title: Projectile Trajectory Analyzer
spec: Write a function `simulate(velocities)` that takes a list of initial vertical speeds in meters per second. For each speed, calculate the time to reach the highest point assuming gravity is nine point eight meters per second squared. Then calculate the maximum height reached. If the height exceeds one hundred meters, classify it as high altitude. Return a list of tuples containing the time, the maximum height, and a boolean indicating if it is high altitude. Example: input of a list containing twenty should output a list with a tuple of roughly two point zero four, twenty point four, and false.

title: Mortgage Amortization Steps
spec: Write a function `amortize(loan)` where the input is a list of three numbers: principal amount, annual interest rate as a decimal, and monthly payment. Calculate the interest for the first month by dividing the annual rate by twelve and multiplying by the principal. Deduct this interest from the monthly payment to find the principal reduction. Subtract the principal reduction from the starting principal to get the new balance. Return a tuple containing the first month interest, the principal paid, and the remaining balance. Example: input of one thousand, zero point twelve, and one hundred should yield ten, ninety, and nine hundred ten.

title: Quadrilateral Metrics
spec: Write a function `metrics(vertices)` that accepts a list of four pairs of numbers representing corner coordinates. Calculate the width as the maximum first coordinate minus the minimum first coordinate. Calculate the height as the maximum second coordinate minus the minimum second coordinate. Find the area of this bounding box by multiplying width and height. Also, check if the width is exactly equal to the height to determine if the bounding box is a square. Return the box area and the square boolean. Example: input of pairs zero zero, zero two, two two, and two zero yields four and true.

title: Statistical Z-Score Calculator
spec: Write a function `normalize(values)` that takes a list of numbers. Find the average by dividing the sum of the numbers by their count. Next, calculate the variance by taking the difference between each number and the average, squaring that difference, summing these squares, and dividing by the count. Compute the standard deviation by taking the square root of the variance. Finally, create a new list where each original number has the average subtracted from it, and that result is divided by the standard deviation. Return this new list. Example: input of two, four, and six returns negative one point two two, zero, and one point two two.

title: Overtime Payroll Processor
spec: Write a function `payroll(hours)` that takes a list of weekly hours worked by employees. For each employee, if their hours are greater than forty, compute the regular pay as forty times twenty, compute the overtime hours as total hours minus forty, and compute overtime pay as overtime hours times thirty. If hours are forty or less, regular pay is hours times twenty and overtime pay is zero. The total pay is regular pay plus overtime pay. Return a list of total pay for each employee. Example: input of thirty and forty five returns six hundred and nine hundred fifty.

title: Retail Price Adjuster
spec: Write a function `checkout(prices)` that accepts a list of item costs. For each item, if the cost is greater than fifty, apply a twenty percent discount. For items fifty or less, apply a ten percent discount. Add the discounted costs together to find the subtotal. Calculate the sales tax by multiplying the subtotal by zero point zero eight. The final total is the subtotal plus the tax. Return a tuple of the subtotal, the tax, and the final total. Example: input of forty and sixty yields eighty four, six point seven two, and ninety point seven two.

title: RPG Combat Damage Resolver
spec: Write a function `combat(stats)` that accepts a list of character stats where each element is a tuple of attack power, target defense, and a base multiplier. For each attack, calculate the net power as attack power minus target defense. If the net power is less than zero, set it to zero. Multiply the net power by the base multiplier to get the gross damage. If the gross damage is greater than one hundred, cap it at one hundred. Return a list of the final damage amounts. Example: input of fifty, thirty, and two yields forty.

title: Temperature Trend Analyzer
spec: Write a function `climate(temperatures)` that takes a list of daily high temperatures in Fahrenheit. For each temperature, subtract thirty two and multiply the result by five ninths to convert to Celsius. Find the highest Celsius temperature and the lowest Celsius temperature in the list. Compute the temperature range by subtracting the lowest from the highest. If the range is greater than fifteen, the weather is considered volatile. Return the highest Celsius value, the range, and the volatile boolean. Example: input of thirty two and fifty yields ten, ten, and false.

title: Fitness Metric Evaluator
spec: Write a function `fitness(profiles)` that takes a list of tuples containing weight in kilograms and height in meters. For each profile, calculate the body mass index by dividing the weight by the square of the height. If the index is less than eighteen point five, classify it as underweight. If it is greater than or equal to twenty five, classify as overweight. Otherwise, it is normal. Return a list of tuples containing the calculated index and the text classification. Example: input of seventy and one point seven five yields twenty two point eight and normal.

title: Freight Cost Estimator
spec: Write a function `freight(packages)` that takes a list of package weights in pounds. The base cost for any package is five dollars. If the weight is greater than ten pounds, add a surcharge of two dollars per pound for every pound over ten. If the weight is greater than fifty pounds, add an additional heavy fee of twenty dollars to the surcharge. The total cost is the base cost plus the surcharge and heavy fee. Return a list of total costs per package. Example: input of five, twelve, and sixty yields five, nine, and one hundred twenty five.

title: Kinetic Energy Comparator
spec: Write a function `energy(objects)` that accepts a list of pairs representing mass in kilograms and velocity in meters per second. For each pair, calculate the kinetic energy by multiplying zero point five by the mass and by the square of the velocity. Find the average energy by summing all calculated energies and dividing by the number of objects. Then count how many objects have an energy strictly greater than the average. Return the average energy and the count of high energy objects. Example: input of two and three, and four and one yields five point five and one.

title: Property Valuation Engine
spec: Write a function `appraise(properties)` that takes a list of tuples containing land area in square feet and house area in square feet. The land value is calculated by multiplying the land area by fifteen. The house value is calculated by multiplying the house area by one hundred fifty. The preliminary value is the sum of land value and house value. If the preliminary value is less than two hundred thousand, add a flat bonus of ten thousand. Return a list of final property values. Example: input of one thousand and one thousand yields one hundred sixty five thousand.

title: Semester GPA Calculator
spec: Write a function `academics(students)` that takes a list of student records, where each record is a list of numeric course grades on a hundred point scale. For each grade, if it is greater than or equal to ninety, it earns four points. If it is greater than or equal to eighty and less than ninety, it earns three points. Otherwise it earns two points. Calculate the student grade point average by summing these points and dividing by the number of courses. Return a list of averages for each student. Example: input of ninety five and eighty five yields three point five.

title: Production Yield Analyzer
spec: Write a function `production(batches)` that takes a list of tuples containing total units started and units rejected. For each batch, calculate the good units by subtracting the rejected units from the total units. Calculate the yield percentage by dividing the good units by the total units and multiplying by one hundred. If the yield percentage is less than ninety five, flag the batch as defective. Return a list of tuples with the good units, the yield percentage, and the defective flag. Example: input of one hundred and five yields ninety five, ninety five, and false.

title: Field Harvest Estimator
spec: Write a function `harvest(fields)` that accepts a list of tuples containing acreage and fertilizer applied in tons. The base yield is fifty bushels per acre. The fertilizer bonus is calculated by multiplying the fertilizer amount by ten. The total yield per acre is the base yield plus the fertilizer bonus. The total field production is the total yield per acre multiplied by the acreage. If the total field production is greater than one thousand, it is a high yield field. Return a list of total productions. Example: input of ten and two yields seven hundred.

title: Foreign Exchange Calculator
spec: Write a function `exchange(transactions)` that takes a list of amounts in foreign currency. The conversion rate is one point two five dollars per foreign unit. A transaction fee of two point five dollars is applied to every exchange. For each amount, multiply it by the conversion rate to get the raw dollar value. Subtract the transaction fee from the raw value to get the net dollars. If the net dollars is less than zero, set it to zero. Return a list of net dollar amounts. Example: input of ten and one yields ten and zero.

title: Daily Power Usage
spec: Write a function `electricity(devices)` that takes a list of tuples containing device wattage and hours used per day. For each device, multiply the wattage by the hours used to get daily watt hours. Divide the daily watt hours by one thousand to convert to kilowatt hours. The daily cost is the kilowatt hours multiplied by zero point fifteen dollars. Sum the daily costs of all devices to find the total daily bill. Return the total daily bill. Example: input of one hundred and ten, and two thousand and one yields zero point four five.

title: Mobile Data Biller
spec: Write a function `billing(accounts)` that takes a list of gigabytes used by different customers. The monthly plan includes five gigabytes for a flat rate of thirty dollars. For every gigabyte strictly greater than five, there is an overage charge of ten dollars per gigabyte. For each account, subtract five from the usage to find the overage amount. If the overage amount is greater than zero, multiply it by ten to get the extra fee, otherwise the extra fee is zero. Return a list of total bills. Example: input of four and seven yields thirty and fifty.

title: Planetary Orbit Analyzer
spec: Write a function `orbit(planets)` that takes a list of tuples containing the closest distance to the sun and the farthest distance to the sun in million kilometers. For each planet, calculate the semi major axis by adding the closest and farthest distances and dividing by two. Calculate the eccentricity by subtracting the closest distance from the farthest distance, and dividing that difference by the sum of the two distances. Return a list of tuples with the semi major axis and the eccentricity. Example: input of ninety and one hundred ten yields one hundred and zero point one.

title: Molarity Dilution Calculator
spec: Write a function `dilution(solutions)` that takes a list of tuples containing initial volume in liters and initial concentration in moles per liter. A target volume of five liters is desired for all solutions. For each solution, calculate the total moles by multiplying the initial volume by the initial concentration. Then find the new concentration by dividing the total moles by the target volume of five. If the new concentration is less than zero point one, it is considered weak. Return a list of the new concentrations. Example: input of two and one yields zero point four.

title: Network Transfer Estimator
spec: Write a function `transfer(files)` that takes a list of file sizes in megabytes. The network speed is twenty megabits per second. To find the transfer time, first multiply the file size by eight to convert megabytes to megabits. Then divide the megabits by the network speed to get the time in seconds. If the time is greater than sixty seconds, calculate the minutes by dividing the time by sixty. Return a list of times in seconds for each file. Example: input of fifty and one hundred yields twenty and forty.

title: Stock Replenishment Logic
spec: Write a function `inventory(items)` that accepts a list of tuples containing current stock, average daily sales, and lead time in days. For each item, calculate the safety stock by multiplying the average daily sales by two. Calculate the reorder point by multiplying the average daily sales by the lead time, and then adding the safety stock. If the current stock is less than or equal to the reorder point, a reorder is needed. Return a list of booleans indicating if a reorder should be placed. Example: input of twenty, five, and three yields true.

title: Real Wage Calculator
spec: Write a function `wages(salaries)` that takes a list of tuples containing starting salary, ending salary, and the inflation rate as a decimal. For each record, calculate the nominal growth by subtracting the starting salary from the ending salary. Divide the nominal growth by the starting salary to find the nominal percentage increase. Subtract the inflation rate from the nominal percentage increase to find the real wage growth. If the real growth is less than zero, purchasing power decreased. Return a list of real wage growth rates. Example: input of fifty thousand, fifty five thousand, and zero point zero five yields zero point zero five.

title: Sound Pressure Analyzer
spec: Write a function `acoustics(pressures)` that takes a list of sound pressures in micropascals. The reference pressure is twenty micropascals. For each value, divide it by the reference pressure to get the pressure ratio. Calculate the logarithm base ten of this ratio, which you can approximate or compute using the math module. Multiply the logarithm result by twenty to find the decibel level. If the decibel level is greater than eighty five, it is considered harmful. Return a list of decibel levels. Example: input of two hundred yields twenty.

title: Species Growth Model
spec: Write a function `population(regions)` that takes a list of tuples containing initial population, birth rate as a decimal, and death rate as a decimal. For each region, calculate the net growth rate by subtracting the death rate from the birth rate. Multiply the initial population by the net growth rate to find the population change. Add the population change to the initial population to get the final population. If the final population is less than the initial population, the species is in decline. Return a list of final populations. Example: input of one hundred, zero point one, and zero point zero five yields one hundred five.

title: Solar Panel Sizing
spec: Provide the entry function `solar(consumption, peak)`. Receive yearly electricity consumption and daily peak sun hours. Calculate daily energy needed by dividing the consumption by three hundred sixty five. Multiply this daily energy by a system loss factor of one point two to get adjusted daily energy. Determine the required array wattage by dividing the adjusted daily energy by the peak sun hours. Calculate the number of solar panels by dividing the array wattage by a standard panel rating of four hundred watts. Check if the required number of panels is less than a strict roof limit of twenty. Return a tuple containing the daily energy, adjusted daily energy, array wattage, number of panels, and the roof limit boolean.

title: Macro Nutrient Breakdown
spec: Provide the entry function `macros(weight, bodyfat)`. Receive weight in pounds and body fat percentage as a decimal. Calculate lean mass by subtracting the bodyfat percentage from one and multiplying the result by the weight. Calculate the base metabolic rate by multiplying the lean mass by thirteen point eight. Determine the daily energy expenditure by multiplying the metabolic rate by an activity factor of one point five. Calculate protein grams by multiplying lean mass by one point two. Find fat grams by multiplying total weight by zero point four. Calculate carbohydrate grams by subtracting the calories of protein and fat (using four and nine calories per gram respectively) from the daily expenditure, then dividing by four. Return a tuple of daily expenditure, protein, fat, and carbohydrates.

title: Coffee Extraction Yield
spec: Provide the entry function `extraction(dose, water)`. Receive ground coffee dose and brewing water weight. Calculate retained water by multiplying the coffee dose by two. Calculate final beverage weight by subtracting the retained water from the brewing water. Determine the total dissolved solids by multiplying the beverage weight by a standard concentration factor of zero point zero one four. Calculate the extraction yield by dividing the dissolved solids by the original coffee dose. Check if the extraction yield is greater than a minimum acceptable threshold of zero point one eight. Check if the yield is less than a maximum threshold of zero point two two. Return a tuple of beverage weight, dissolved solids, extraction yield, and the two threshold booleans.

title: Scuba Gas Planning
spec: Provide the entry function `dive(depth, rate)`. Receive dive depth in meters and surface air consumption rate. Calculate ambient pressure by dividing the depth by ten and adding one. Calculate the depth consumption rate by multiplying the surface rate by the ambient pressure. Determine the gas needed for the bottom phase by multiplying the depth consumption rate by a planned time of forty five minutes. Calculate a reserve gas amount by multiplying the surface rate by ambient pressure and an ascent factor of five. Find total required gas by adding the bottom gas and reserve gas. Check if the total gas is less than a standard tank capacity of two thousand liters. Return a tuple of ambient pressure, depth consumption rate, bottom gas, reserve gas, total required gas, and the capacity boolean.

title: Concrete Volume Estimator
spec: Provide the entry function `concrete(length, width)`. Receive slab length and width in feet. Calculate the surface area by multiplying the length by the width. Calculate cubic feet by multiplying the surface area by a standard depth of zero point five feet. Convert the cubic feet to cubic yards by dividing by twenty seven. Add a waste margin by multiplying the cubic yards by one point one. Calculate the required bags of cement by multiplying the adjusted cubic yards by forty five. Check if the required bags are less than a bulk delivery threshold of one hundred. Return a tuple of surface area, cubic feet, cubic yards, bags required, and the threshold boolean.

title: Bicycle Gearing and Speed
spec: Provide the entry function `gearing(chainring, cog)`. Receive tooth counts for the front chainring and rear cog. Calculate the gear ratio by dividing the front count by the rear count. Calculate gear inches by multiplying the ratio by a standard wheel diameter of twenty seven. Determine the development in meters by multiplying gear inches by zero point zero eight. Calculate the bike speed in kilometers per hour by multiplying the development by a cadence of ninety, multiplying by sixty, and dividing by one thousand. Check if this speed exceeds a cruising threshold of thirty. Return a tuple of gear ratio, gear inches, development, speed, and the threshold boolean.

title: Aquarium Heater Sizing
spec: Provide the entry function `aquarium(gallons, ambient)`. Receive tank volume in gallons and ambient room temperature. Calculate water volume in liters by multiplying gallons by three point seven eight. Calculate the temperature difference by subtracting the ambient temperature from a target tropical temperature of seventy eight. Calculate the baseline heating power by multiplying the volume by the temperature difference and a specific heat constant of zero point two. Add a heat loss buffer by multiplying the power by one point two five. Determine if a secondary heater is needed by checking if the buffered power is greater than a single heater maximum limit of three hundred. Return a tuple of water volume, temperature difference, baseline power, buffered power, and the secondary heater boolean.

title: Room Paint Estimator
spec: Provide the entry function `paint(perimeter, height)`. Receive room perimeter and ceiling height in feet. Calculate total wall area by multiplying the perimeter by the height. Subtract a fixed door area of twenty one and a fixed window area of fifteen from the total wall area to find the paintable surface. Calculate the required paint volume in gallons by dividing the paintable surface by a standard coverage rate of three hundred and fifty. Multiply the volume by two to account for a necessary second coat. Calculate the number of cans to purchase by rounding the volume up to the nearest whole integer using standard arithmetic or math logic. Check if the number of cans is greater than or equal to a bulk discount threshold of five. Return a tuple of paintable surface, gallons, cans, and the discount boolean.

title: Flight Descent Profile
spec: Provide the entry function `descent(cruise, target)`. Receive current cruise altitude and destination airport altitude in feet. Calculate the total altitude to lose by subtracting the target altitude from the cruise altitude. Determine the time required for descent by dividing the altitude to lose by a standard descent rate of five hundred feet per minute. Calculate the distance traveled during descent by multiplying the time required by a standard ground speed of three miles per minute. Add a level off buffer distance by multiplying the calculated distance by one point one. Check if the total required distance is less than a maximum allowed airspace range of fifty miles. Return a tuple of altitude to lose, descent time, calculated distance, buffered distance, and the range boolean.

title: Running Race Pacer
spec: Provide the entry function `pace(distance, goal)`. Receive race distance in miles and total goal time in minutes. Calculate the average pace per mile by dividing the goal time by the distance. Calculate the halfway split time by dividing the goal time by two. Calculate a negative split target by subtracting one point five minutes from the halfway split time for the second half. Calculate the required average speed in miles per hour by dividing sixty by the average pace. Check if the required speed is greater than a qualifying threshold speed of eight miles per hour. Return a tuple of average pace, halfway split, second half target, required speed, and the threshold boolean.

title: Electric Vehicle Trip Range
spec: Provide the entry function `evtrip(capacity, efficiency)`. Receive battery capacity in kilowatt hours and baseline efficiency in miles per unit. Calculate the theoretical range by multiplying the capacity by the efficiency. Subtract a highway driving penalty by multiplying the theoretical range by zero point eight five. Subtract a cold weather penalty by multiplying the highway adjusted range by zero point nine. Calculate the usable trip range by subtracting a safe arrival buffer of twenty miles from the weather adjusted range. Check if the usable trip range is greater than a required distance of one hundred and fifty miles. Return a tuple of theoretical range, highway adjusted range, usable trip range, and the distance boolean.

title: Crop Irrigation Estimator
spec: Provide the entry function `irrigation(area, loss)`. Receive field area in acres and daily water loss in inches. Calculate the gross water requirement by multiplying the daily loss by a crop coefficient of one point two. Subtract an average natural rainfall of zero point one inches from the gross requirement to get the net irrigation depth. Calculate the total water volume in acre inches by multiplying the area by the net irrigation depth. Convert the volume to gallons by multiplying by twenty seven thousand one hundred and fifty four. Calculate the pump run time in hours by dividing the total gallons by a pump flow rate of five hundred gallons per hour. Check if the run time is less than a maximum daylight limit of twelve hours. Return a tuple of net irrigation depth, total volume in acre inches, total gallons, run time, and the daylight limit boolean.

title: Tire Circumference and Speedometer Error
spec: Provide the entry function `tires(width, aspect)`. Receive tire width in millimeters and aspect ratio as a whole number percentage. Calculate the sidewall height by multiplying the width by the aspect ratio and dividing by one hundred. Convert the sidewall height to inches by dividing by twenty five point four. Calculate the total tire diameter by multiplying the sidewall inches by two and adding a standard wheel diameter of eighteen inches. Calculate the tire circumference by multiplying the diameter by three point one four one five. Calculate revolutions per mile by dividing sixty three thousand three hundred and sixty by the circumference. Check if the revolutions per mile is less than a factory limit of eight hundred. Return a tuple of sidewall inches, diameter, circumference, revolutions per mile, and the limit boolean.

title: Bakery Recipe Scaler
spec: Provide the entry function `scale(flour, hydration)`. Receive original flour weight and desired hydration percentage as a whole number. Calculate the original water weight by multiplying the flour by the hydration and dividing by one hundred. Calculate the total original dough weight by adding the flour, the water, and fixed amounts of ten grams for salt and five grams for yeast. Determine a scaling factor by dividing a target production weight of two thousand grams by the total original dough weight. Calculate the new flour weight by multiplying the original flour by the scaling factor. Calculate the new water weight by multiplying the original water by the scaling factor. Check if the new flour weight exceeds a mixing bowl capacity of one thousand two hundred grams. Return a tuple of total original weight, scaling factor, new flour, new water, and the capacity boolean.

title: Tax Bracket Estimator
spec: Provide the entry function `taxes(income, deduction)`. Receive gross income and standard deduction amounts. Calculate taxable income by subtracting the deduction from the gross income. Calculate base tax by multiplying a lower income threshold of fifty thousand by a standard low tax rate of zero point one. Calculate remaining income by subtracting the lower threshold from the taxable income. Calculate excess tax by multiplying the remaining income by a higher marginal tax rate of zero point two. Calculate total tax by adding the base tax and excess tax. Calculate the effective tax rate by dividing the total tax by the gross income. Check if the effective rate is below a target percentage of zero point one five. Return a tuple of taxable income, remaining income, total tax, effective rate, and the target boolean.

title: HVAC Cooling Load
spec: Provide the entry function `hvac(area, occupants)`. Receive room square footage and number of regular occupants. Calculate base cooling load in btus by multiplying the area by thirty. Calculate the occupant load by multiplying the number of people by four hundred. Add the base load and occupant load to get the subtotal cooling required. Add a solar heat gain by multiplying a constant window area of fifty square feet by a specific solar factor of twenty. Calculate the total required cooling by adding the solar gain to the subtotal. Check if the total cooling is less than a standard portable air conditioner rating of eight thousand btus. Return a tuple of base load, occupant load, subtotal cooling, total required cooling, and the rating boolean.

title: Brewing Alcohol Content
spec: Provide the entry function `alcohol(original, final)`. Receive original specific gravity and final specific gravity. Calculate the gravity drop by subtracting the final gravity from the original gravity. Calculate alcohol by volume by multiplying the gravity drop by one hundred and thirty one point two five. Calculate calories from alcohol by multiplying the alcohol by volume by twenty four. Calculate calories from sugars by multiplying the final gravity by ten. Find total calories by adding the alcohol calories and sugar calories. Check if the alcohol by volume is greater than a threshold of seven. Return a tuple of gravity drop, alcohol by volume, total calories, and the threshold boolean.

title: Wind Turbine Power Generation
spec: Provide the entry function `turbine(speed, radius)`. Receive wind speed in meters per second and blade radius in meters. Calculate the swept area by multiplying the radius by the radius and then by three point one four. Calculate the wind power potential by multiplying an air density of one point two by the swept area and by the wind speed cubed, then dividing the entire result by two. Calculate the actual mechanical power by multiplying the potential by a standard turbine efficiency factor of zero point four. Calculate electrical output by multiplying the mechanical power by a generator efficiency of zero point nine. Check if the electrical output exceeds a minimum grid connection threshold of five thousand watts. Return a tuple of swept area, power potential, actual mechanical power, electrical output, and the threshold boolean.

title: Pool Chemical Dosing
spec: Provide the entry function `pool(volume, current)`. Receive pool volume in gallons and current chlorine level in parts per million. Calculate the chlorine deficit by subtracting the current level from a target ideal level of three. Calculate the volume factor by dividing the volume by ten thousand. Determine required ounces of chemical by multiplying the chlorine deficit by the volume factor and a standard dosage multiplier of two point five. Calculate the maintenance acid dose by multiplying the volume factor by a standard weekly acid amount of ten. Calculate total maintenance cost by adding the cost of chlorine (ounces multiplied by zero point five) and acid (dose multiplied by zero point two). Check if the total cost is below a weekly budget of twenty dollars. Return a tuple of chlorine deficit, volume factor, chemical ounces, acid dose, total cost, and the budget boolean.

title: Flash Guide Number Distance
spec: Provide the entry function `flash(guide, aperture)`. Receive flash guide number and lens aperture. Calculate maximum subject distance by dividing the guide number by the aperture. Calculate the near distance limit by multiplying the maximum distance by a fractional constant of zero point three. Calculate total depth of flash range by subtracting the near limit from the maximum distance. Calculate the required recycle time by multiplying the maximum distance by a standard power recharge factor of zero point five. Check if the recycle time is less than a rapid fire limit of two seconds. Return a tuple of maximum distance, near limit, total depth of flash range, recycle time, and the rapid fire boolean.

title: Water Pipe Flow Rate
spec: Provide the entry function `flow(pressure, diameter)`. Receive water pressure and pipe diameter. Calculate the pipe cross section area by multiplying the diameter by the diameter, multiplying by three point one four, and dividing by four. Calculate fluid velocity by multiplying the pressure by a standard flow coefficient of zero point eight. Determine the raw flow rate by multiplying the cross section area by the fluid velocity. Apply a friction loss factor by multiplying the raw flow rate by a pipe material constant of zero point nine. Calculate daily volume by multiplying the final flow rate by eighty six thousand four hundred. Check if the daily volume exceeds a community usage limit of five thousand. Return a tuple of cross section area, fluid velocity, final flow rate, daily volume, and the limit boolean.

title: Video Game Experience Tracker
spec: Provide the entry function `experience(kills, quests)`. Receive number of monster kills and completed quests. Calculate combat experience by multiplying kills by fifty. Calculate quest experience by multiplying quests by two hundred. Add the combat and quest experience to get total earned experience. Calculate the current level by dividing the total experience by one thousand and rounding down or truncating to a whole integer. Calculate the remaining experience towards the next level by finding the remainder when total experience is divided by one thousand. Check if the current level is greater than a veteran threshold of ten. Return a tuple of combat experience, quest experience, total earned experience, current level, remaining experience, and the threshold boolean.

title: Coffee Roasting Weight Loss
spec: Provide the entry function `roasting(green, moisture)`. Receive green coffee weight and original moisture percentage. Calculate the moisture loss by multiplying the green weight by the moisture percentage and dividing by one hundred. Calculate the dry weight by subtracting the moisture loss from the green weight. Determine the chaff loss by multiplying the dry weight by a standard chaff factor of zero point zero two. Calculate the roasted weight by subtracting the chaff loss from the dry weight. Calculate the total weight loss percentage by subtracting the roasted weight from the green weight, then dividing by the green weight. Check if the total weight loss is less than a maximum acceptable roasting threshold of zero point two. Return a tuple of moisture loss, dry weight, chaff loss, roasted weight, total weight loss percentage, and the threshold boolean.

title: Real Estate Rental Yield
spec: Provide the entry function `rental(price, rent)`. Receive property purchase price and monthly rent. Calculate annual rental income by multiplying the monthly rent by twelve. Calculate annual property taxes by multiplying the purchase price by a standard tax rate of zero point zero one five. Calculate annual maintenance cost by multiplying the purchase price by a standard upkeep percentage of zero point zero one. Calculate net operating income by subtracting taxes and maintenance from the annual rental income. Calculate the gross yield by dividing the annual rental income by the purchase price. Check if the net operating income is greater than a positive cash flow target of five thousand. Return a tuple of annual rental income, taxes, maintenance, net operating income, gross yield, and the target boolean.

title: Soil Fertilizer Blend
spec: Provide the entry function `fertilizer(nitrogen, area)`. Receive target nitrogen in pounds per acre and total field area in acres. Calculate total nitrogen needed by multiplying the target rate by the area. Calculate the number of bags of primary fertilizer by dividing the total nitrogen by a standard bag nitrogen content of ten. Calculate phosphorus provided by multiplying the bags by a bag phosphorus content of five. Calculate potassium provided by multiplying the bags by a bag potassium content of five. Calculate total weight applied by multiplying the bags by a standard bag weight of fifty. Check if the total weight is less than a tractor payload limit of two thousand. Return a tuple of total nitrogen, bags needed, phosphorus provided, potassium provided, total weight, and the payload boolean.

title: Lens Focal Length Calculator
spec: Write a function `optics(parameters)` that takes a list containing three numbers: the radii of curvature for the front and back surfaces of a lens in millimeters, and the refractive index of the glass. Calculate the inverse focal length by subtracting one from the refractive index, and multiplying that result by the difference of one divided by the front radius and one divided by the back radius. Calculate the focal length by taking the reciprocal of the inverse focal length. Calculate the optical power in diopters by dividing one thousand by the focal length. If the focal length is positive, classify the lens as the string converging, otherwise as diverging. Return a tuple containing the focal length rounded to one decimal, the power rounded to two decimals, and the classification string. Example: given 10.0, -15.0, and 1.5, return 12.0, 83.33, and converging.

title: Rocket Delta-V Calculator
spec: Write a function `propulsion(stages)` that takes a list of lists, where each inner list represents a rocket stage and contains three numbers: empty mass, propellant mass, and specific impulse. For each stage, calculate the initial total mass by adding empty and propellant mass, then calculate the mass ratio by dividing initial mass by empty mass. Multiply the specific impulse by nine point eight to get exhaust velocity, then multiply by the natural logarithm of the mass ratio to find the stage's velocity change. Accumulate these velocity changes to find the total vehicle capability. Return a list containing the total velocity change rounded to the nearest integer, and a string classifying the rocket as orbital if the total exceeds nine thousand three hundred, or suborbital otherwise. Example: given a single stage with 1000, 9000, and 300, return 6769 and suborbital.

title: Photography Depth of Field
spec: Write a function `hyperfocal(settings)` that receives four numbers: lens focal length in millimeters, aperture f-number, subject distance in millimeters, and circle of confusion in millimeters. Calculate the hyperfocal distance by squaring the focal length and dividing by the product of aperture and circle of confusion, then adding the focal length. Calculate the near limit by multiplying hyperfocal distance by subject distance, then dividing by the sum of hyperfocal distance and subject distance minus focal length. Calculate the far limit similarly, but dividing by the difference between hyperfocal distance and subject distance minus focal length. If the denominator for the far limit is zero or negative, set the far limit to infinity. Return a tuple with hyperfocal distance, near limit, and far limit, all rounded to one decimal place. Example: given 50, 8, 5000, and 0.03, return 10466.7, 3384.7, and 9545.5.

title: Epidemic SIR Model
spec: Write a function `outbreak(population)` that takes an initial population size, initial infected count, transmission rate, recovery rate, and a number of days to simulate. The initial susceptible count is the population size minus infected, and recovered starts at zero. For each day, calculate new infections by multiplying the transmission rate, susceptible count, and infected count, then dividing by total population. Calculate new recoveries by multiplying recovery rate by infected count. Update the susceptible, infected, and recovered pools by adding or subtracting these new daily values. If the infected count drops below one, stop the simulation early. Return a tuple of the final susceptible, infected, and recovered counts, each rounded to the nearest integer. Example: given 1000, 10, 0.3, 0.1, and 5, return 967, 33, and 1.

title: Elevator Counterweight Sizing
spec: Write a function `elevator(specs)` that takes the empty mass of an elevator cab, its maximum passenger capacity mass, the mass of the hoisting cable, and the suspension ratio. Calculate the ideal counterweight mass, which is the cab mass plus half of the passenger capacity mass. Calculate the maximum motor load when lifting a fully loaded cab, which is the cab plus capacity plus cable minus the counterweight, all divided by the suspension ratio. Calculate the minimum motor load when lifting an empty cab, which is the cab plus cable minus the counterweight, divided by the ratio. Return a list of three numbers rounded to one decimal place: counterweight mass, maximum positive motor load, and maximum negative motor load. Example: given 1000, 800, 100, and 2, return 1400.0, 250.0, and -150.0.

title: Ice Cream Mix Balancing
spec: Write a function `creamery(ingredients)` that receives a target batch weight in grams and target percentages for butterfat, serum solids, and sugar as decimals. The ingredients available are heavy cream which is forty percent fat and five percent serum solids, skim milk powder which is ninety six percent serum solids, and pure sugar. Calculate the required grams of sugar by multiplying batch weight by sugar percentage. Set up a balance for the fat to find the grams of cream needed by dividing the target fat mass by zero point four zero. Calculate the serum solids contributed by the cream, subtract it from the total target serum solids, and divide the remainder by zero point nine six to find the grams of skim milk powder required. The rest of the batch weight is made up of water. Return a list of four numbers rounded to the nearest integer: grams of cream, skim milk powder, sugar, and water. Example: given 1000, 0.15, 0.10, and 0.15, return 375, 85, 150, and 390.

title: Atmospheric Pressure Altitude
spec: Write a function `altitude(conditions)` that accepts the station pressure in millibars, the station elevation in meters, and the current temperature in celsius. Convert the temperature to kelvin by adding two hundred seventy three point fifteen. Calculate the sea level pressure equivalent by multiplying the station pressure by the mathematical constant e raised to the power of a fraction: the station elevation times zero point zero three four one six, divided by the temperature in kelvin. Then calculate the pressure altitude by subtracting the station pressure from one thousand thirteen point twenty five, multiplying the difference by twenty seven point three, and adding the station elevation. Return a tuple of the sea level pressure and pressure altitude, both rounded to one decimal place. Example: given 800, 2000, and 15, return 1013.8 and 7821.7.

title: Drone Flight Time Estimator
spec: Write a function `quadcopter(specs)` that takes the battery capacity in milliamp hours, battery voltage, drone empty weight in grams, payload weight in grams, and motor efficiency in grams per watt. Calculate the total energy in watt hours by multiplying capacity and voltage, then dividing by one thousand. Calculate the total weight by adding empty weight and payload weight. Calculate the electrical power required to hover by dividing the total weight by the motor efficiency. Calculate the theoretical hover time in minutes by dividing the total energy by the hover power, then multiplying by sixty. Subtract a twenty percent safety margin from the theoretical time to get the safe flight time. Return a list containing the hover power rounded to one decimal and safe flight time rounded to the nearest integer. Example: given 5000, 15, 1000, 500, and 10, return 150.0 and 24.

title: Carpet Roll Optimisation
spec: Write a function `flooring(dimensions)` that accepts a room length in meters, room width in meters, carpet roll width in meters, and a pattern repeat length in meters. Calculate the number of strips needed by dividing the room width by the roll width, rounding up to the nearest whole number. Calculate the effective strip length by adding the pattern repeat to the room length. Multiply the effective strip length by the number of strips to get the total linear meters of carpet required. Calculate the total area of carpet purchased, and subtract the actual room area to find the waste area. Return a list containing the number of strips, total linear meters, and the waste area rounded to two decimals. Example: given 5.0, 4.0, 4.0, and 1.0, return 1, 6.0, and 4.0.

title: Hydraulic Press Force
spec: Write a function `hydraulics(system)` that takes the diameter of the input pump cylinder in centimeters, the diameter of the output press cylinder in centimeters, the force applied to the pump in newtons, and the stroke length of the pump in centimeters. Calculate the area of both cylinders using the formula pi times the radius squared. Calculate the fluid pressure by dividing the input force by the input area. Calculate the output force by multiplying the pressure by the output area. Calculate the output stroke length by multiplying the input stroke length by the input area, then dividing by the output area. Return a tuple containing the fluid pressure, output force, and output stroke length, all rounded to two decimals. Example: given 10, 50, 100, and 20, return 1.27, 2500.0, and 0.8.

title: Radio Antenna Length
spec: Write a function `antenna(frequency)` that accepts a target transmission frequency in megahertz and a velocity factor for the antenna wire material as a decimal. Calculate the full wavelength in free space by dividing three hundred by the frequency. Calculate the physical length of a half wave dipole by dividing the full wavelength by two, then multiplying by the velocity factor. Calculate the physical length of a quarter wave vertical monopole by dividing the full wavelength by four, then multiplying by the velocity factor. If the frequency is greater than thirty, the antenna is considered very high frequency; otherwise, it is high frequency. Return a list with the free space wavelength, dipole length, monopole length, and the classification string, all lengths rounded to three decimals. Example: given 100 and 0.95, return 3.0, 1.425, 0.713, and very high frequency.

title: Cheese Ripening Shrinkage
spec: Write a function `cheese(batch)` that takes the fresh weight of a cheese wheel in kilograms, the initial moisture percentage as a decimal, the daily evaporation rate as a decimal, and the aging duration in days. Calculate the initial moisture mass by multiplying the fresh weight by the initial moisture percentage. Calculate the daily mass lost by multiplying the initial moisture mass by the evaporation rate. Calculate the total mass lost over the aging duration. Calculate the final wheel weight by subtracting the total mass lost from the fresh weight. Calculate the final moisture mass by subtracting the total mass lost from the initial moisture mass, and find the new moisture percentage by dividing the final moisture mass by the final wheel weight. Return a tuple containing the final weight and final moisture percentage rounded to two decimal places. Example: given 10, 0.4, 0.01, and 30, return 8.8 and 0.32.

title: Warehouse Pallet Racking
spec: Write a function `warehouse(layout)` that receives a total building width in meters, building length in meters, aisle width in meters, pallet width in meters, pallet depth in meters, and maximum racking height in meters. Calculate the footprint of one rack row by adding the pallet depth and a small rear clearance of zero point one meters. Calculate the space required for one aisle and one rack row. Divide the building width by this combined space to find the total number of rack rows, rounding down to the nearest integer. Calculate the number of bays per row by dividing the building length by the pallet width plus zero point one meters clearance, rounding down. Calculate the vertical levels by dividing the racking height by one point five meters, rounding down. Multiply the rows, bays, and levels to find total pallet capacity and return it as an integer. Example: given 50, 100, 3, 1.2, 1.2, and 6, return 2912.

title: Ski Lift Capacity
spec: Write a function `chairlift(specs)` that takes the horizontal length of the lift line in meters, the vertical rise in meters, the lift operating speed in meters per second, the spacing between chairs in meters, and the number of passengers per chair. Calculate the slope length by using the pythagorean theorem with horizontal length and vertical rise. Calculate the ride time in minutes by dividing the slope length by the speed, then dividing by sixty. Calculate the total number of chairs on the entire loop by multiplying the slope length by two, then dividing by the chair spacing. Calculate the hourly passenger capacity by dividing three thousand six hundred by the time interval between chairs, then multiplying by the passengers per chair, where the time interval is chair spacing divided by speed. Return a tuple of ride time, total chairs, and hourly capacity, rounded to one decimal place. Example: given 1000, 300, 2.5, 15, and 4, return 7.0, 139.2, and 2400.0.

title: Solar Eclipse Duration
spec: Write a function `eclipse(data)` that takes the moon shadow diameter on Earth in kilometers, the orbital velocity of the moon in kilometers per second, the rotational velocity of the Earth at the specific latitude in kilometers per second, and the distance to the moon in kilometers. Calculate the relative speed of the shadow across the surface by subtracting the Earth rotational velocity from the moon orbital velocity. Calculate the maximum duration of totality in seconds by dividing the shadow diameter by the relative speed. Calculate the width of the penumbra by multiplying the moon distance by zero point zero zero nine, representing the solar angular diameter. Return a tuple containing the relative speed, totality duration, and penumbra width, all rounded to one decimal place. Example: given 100, 1.0, 0.4, and 380000, return 0.6, 166.7, and 3420.0.

title: Camera Sensor Crop Factor
spec: Write a function `sensor(dimensions)` that takes a target sensor width and height in millimeters, and a lens focal length in millimeters. Calculate the diagonal of the target sensor using the pythagorean theorem. A standard full frame sensor has a width of thirty six and a height of twenty four; calculate its diagonal as well. Calculate the crop factor by dividing the full frame diagonal by the target sensor diagonal. Calculate the equivalent focal length by multiplying the input focal length by the crop factor. Calculate the equivalent aperture depth of field factor by multiplying a standard aperture of two point eight by the crop factor. Return a tuple containing the crop factor, equivalent focal length, and equivalent aperture, rounded to two decimal places. Example: given 24, 16, and 50, return 1.5, 75.0, and 4.2.

title: Battery Bank Sizing
spec: Write a function `offgrid(requirements)` that accepts a daily energy usage in watt hours, a system voltage, a number of autonomy days, a depth of discharge limit as a decimal, and an inverter efficiency as a decimal. Calculate the total daily energy drawn from the battery by dividing the daily usage by the inverter efficiency. Calculate the required usable energy by multiplying the total daily draw by the autonomy days. Calculate the total gross energy storage needed by dividing the usable energy by the depth of discharge limit. Calculate the required battery capacity in amp hours by dividing the gross energy storage by the system voltage. Return a tuple containing the total daily draw, gross energy storage, and amp hour capacity, all rounded to the nearest whole number. Example: given 5000, 48, 3, 0.8, and 0.95, return 5263, 19737, and 411.

title: Gutter Downspout Drainage
spec: Write a function `drainage(roof)` that takes a roof length in meters, a roof width in meters, a roof pitch multiplier, and a rainfall intensity in millimeters per hour. Calculate the effective roof area by multiplying length, width, and the pitch multiplier. Calculate the volume of runoff water in liters per hour by multiplying the effective area by the rainfall intensity. Convert the runoff volume to liters per minute by dividing by sixty. A standard downspout handles two hundred and fifty liters per minute; calculate the number of downspouts required by dividing the liters per minute by two hundred and fifty, and rounding up to the nearest integer. Calculate the spacing between downspouts by dividing the roof perimeter by the number of downspouts. Return a list with the total liters per minute, number of downspouts, and spacing rounded to two decimals. Example: given 10, 8, 1.2, and 50, return 80.0, 1, and 36.0.

title: Train Stopping Distance
spec: Write a function `braking(train)` that accepts a train mass in metric tons, an initial velocity in kilometers per hour, a track grade as a percentage, and a braking friction coefficient. Convert the mass to kilograms by multiplying by one thousand, and velocity to meters per second by dividing by three point six. Calculate the kinetic energy by multiplying half the mass by the square of the velocity. Calculate the gravitational force component by multiplying the mass, nine point eight, and the track grade divided by one hundred. Calculate the braking force by multiplying the mass, nine point eight, and the friction coefficient. The net stopping force is the braking force minus the gravitational force. If the net force is zero or negative, return a string indicating a runaway train, otherwise calculate braking distance by dividing kinetic energy by net force and return the net force and distance rounded to one decimal. Example: given 500, 80, -2, and 0.05, return 147000.0 and 839.8.

title: Aquaponics Fish Density
spec: Write a function `aquaponics(system)` that takes a fish tank volume in liters, an average adult fish mass in grams, a feeding rate as a percentage of body weight, and a biofilter processing rate in grams of ammonia per square meter. Calculate the maximum number of fish the tank can hold by dividing the tank volume by twenty. Calculate the total fish mass in kilograms by multiplying the number of fish by the adult mass, then dividing by one thousand. Calculate the daily feed amount in grams by multiplying the total fish mass in grams by the feeding rate divided by one hundred. Calculate the daily ammonia produced by multiplying the daily feed by zero point zero three. Calculate the required biofilter surface area by dividing the daily ammonia by the processing rate. Return a list with the total fish count, daily feed in grams, and required biofilter area rounded to two decimals. Example: given 1000, 500, 2.0, and 0.5, return 50, 500.0, and 30.0.

title: Helicopter Rotor Lift
spec: Write a function `rotor(specs)` that accepts a main rotor radius in meters, a rotational speed in revolutions per minute, an air density in kilograms per cubic meter, and a lift coefficient. Calculate the rotor disc area using pi times the radius squared. Convert the rotational speed to angular velocity in radians per second by multiplying by pi and dividing by thirty. Calculate the blade tip speed by multiplying the angular velocity by the radius. Calculate the total dynamic pressure by multiplying one half, the air density, and the square of the blade tip speed. Calculate the total lift force by multiplying the dynamic pressure, the disc area, and the lift coefficient. Calculate the maximum lifting capacity in kilograms by dividing the total lift force by nine point eight. Return a tuple of the tip speed, lift force, and maximum capacity, all rounded to two decimal places.

title: Woodworking Board Feet
spec: Write a function `lumber(dimensions)` that accepts a list of lists, where each inner list represents a batch of wooden boards and contains the quantity, thickness in inches, width in inches, length in feet, and a price per board foot. For each batch, calculate the board feet of a single piece by multiplying thickness, width, and length, then dividing by twelve. Calculate the total board feet for the batch by multiplying the single piece board feet by the quantity. Calculate the cost of the batch by multiplying the total board feet by the price. Accumulate the board feet and costs across all batches. If the total board feet exceeds one hundred, apply a ten percent discount to the total accumulated cost. Return a list containing the total board feet and final cost, rounded to two decimal places. Example: given one batch of 10, 2, 6, 8, and 5, return 80.0 and 400.0.

title: Sailboat Hull Speed
spec: Write a function `sailboat(measurements)` that takes a waterline length in feet, a beam width in feet, a draft depth in feet, and a displacement in pounds. Calculate the theoretical hull speed in knots by multiplying one point three four by the square root of the waterline length. Calculate the displacement to length ratio by dividing the displacement divided by two thousand two hundred and forty by the cube of the waterline length divided by one hundred. Calculate the sail area to displacement ratio by using a nominal sail area equal to waterline length times beam width, divided by the displacement in cubic feet raised to the power of two thirds, where a cubic foot of seawater weighs sixty four pounds. Return a tuple containing the hull speed, displacement to length ratio, and sail area ratio, all rounded to two decimal places. Example: given 36, 12, 6, and 20000, return 8.04, 192.9, and 9.4.

title: Telescope Magnification
spec: Write a function `telescope(optics)` that takes an objective lens diameter in millimeters, an objective focal length in millimeters, and an eyepiece focal length in millimeters. Calculate the focal ratio of the telescope by dividing the objective focal length by the objective diameter. Calculate the magnification by dividing the objective focal length by the eyepiece focal length. Calculate the exit pupil diameter by dividing the objective diameter by the magnification. Calculate the maximum useful magnification, which is generally twice the objective diameter. Calculate the resolving power in arcseconds by dividing one hundred and sixteen by the objective diameter. Return a tuple of the focal ratio, magnification, exit pupil, maximum useful magnification, and resolving power, all rounded to one decimal place. Example: given 200, 2000, and 10, return 10.0, 200.0, 1.0, 400.0, and 0.6.

title: Parking Lot Paving
spec: Write a function `paving(lot)` that takes a lot length in meters, a lot width in meters, a required asphalt thickness in centimeters, and a gravel subbase thickness in centimeters. Calculate the total surface area by multiplying length and width. Convert the thicknesses to meters by dividing by one hundred. Calculate the volume of asphalt needed by multiplying the area by the asphalt thickness in meters, and the volume of gravel needed by multiplying the area by the gravel thickness in meters. The density of compacted asphalt is two thousand four hundred kilograms per cubic meter, and gravel is two thousand kilograms per cubic meter. Calculate the total weight of asphalt and gravel in metric tons by multiplying their respective volumes by their densities and dividing by one thousand. Return a list of the asphalt volume in cubic meters, asphalt weight in tons, and gravel weight in tons, all rounded to two decimals. Example: given 100, 50, 10, and 20, return 500.0, 1200.0, and 2000.0.

title: Astronomical Redshift Calculator
spec: Write a function `redshift(wavelength, rest, hubble)` that calculates properties of a galaxy based on its observed wavelength and rest wavelength. First calculate the redshift value as the observed minus the rest, divided by the rest. Then calculate the recession velocity by multiplying the redshift by the speed of light which is three hundred thousand. Next calculate the estimated distance by dividing the velocity by the hubble constant. Finally determine if the galaxy is highly distant by checking if the redshift is greater than zero point five. Return a list containing the redshift, velocity, distance, and a boolean for highly distant. For example given 500, 400, and 70, the output is 0.25, 75000, 1071.4, and false.

title: Credit Score Builder
spec: Provide a function `credit(history, utilization, age, inquiries)` that builds a simulated credit score from base factors. Start with a base score of three hundred. Add the history percentage multiplied by two point five. Subtract the utilization percentage multiplied by one point five. Add the account age in years multiplied by five. Subtract the number of inquiries multiplied by ten. Determine the risk tier: if the final score is less than six hundred return high risk, if it is greater than or equal to seven hundred return low risk, otherwise return medium risk. Return a list of the final score and the risk tier string. For example given 98, 10, 5, 2, the score is 535 and the tier is high risk.

title: Pizza Dough Recipe Balancer
spec: Create a function `dough(flour, hydration, salt, yeast)` to calculate ingredient weights in grams for a pizza recipe. The hydration, salt, and yeast are given as percentages of the flour weight. Calculate the water weight by multiplying the flour by the hydration divided by one hundred. Calculate the salt weight by multiplying the flour by the salt divided by one hundred. Calculate the yeast weight similarly. Find the total dough weight by summing all four ingredient weights. If the hydration is greater than sixty five, classify it as a wet dough, otherwise a standard dough. Return a tuple with the water, salt, yeast, total weight, and the classification string. Example inputs 1000, 70, 2, 1 yield 700, 20, 10, 1730, and wet dough.

title: Blood Alcohol Content Estimator
spec: Write a function `bac(drinks, weight, male, hours)` where male is a boolean indicating if the person is male. The gender factor is zero point seven three if male is true, and zero point six six if false. Calculate total grams of alcohol by multiplying drinks by fourteen. Calculate distribution volume by multiplying weight in kilograms by the gender factor. Calculate the raw level by dividing the alcohol by the volume, then multiplying by eight. Subtract the metabolized amount which is hours multiplied by fifteen. If the final level is less than zero, set it to zero. Return the final level and a boolean indicating if it is greater than or equal to eighty. Example inputs 10, 80, true, 1 yields 4.1 and false.

title: Pendulum Period and Energy
spec: Implement `pendulum(length, mass, angle, gravity)` to compute physical properties of a swinging pendulum. Calculate the standard period by multiplying two by pi and by the square root of the length divided by gravity. Calculate the maximum height reached by subtracting the cosine of the angle in radians from one, then multiplying by the length. Calculate the maximum potential energy by multiplying mass, gravity, and the maximum height. Determine if the small angle approximation is valid by checking if the angle in degrees is less than fifteen. Return a list of period, max height, energy, and the valid boolean. Example 2.0, 1.5, 10, 9.81 yields 2.83, 0.03, 0.44, true.

title: Vehicle Depreciation Profiler
spec: Create a function `depreciation(price, salvage, years, age)` to evaluate the current value of a vehicle. Calculate the straight line yearly drop by subtracting the salvage from the price and dividing by the years. Calculate the straight line value by subtracting the product of the yearly drop and the age from the price. Calculate the double declining rate by dividing two by the years. Calculate the double declining value by multiplying the price by one minus the rate raised to the power of the age. If either calculated value is less than the salvage, set it equal to the salvage. Return a tuple containing the straight line value and the double declining value. Example inputs 20000, 2000, 10, 3 yields 14600 and 10240.

title: Optical Lens Image Solver
spec: Write `optics(focal, object, height)` to find image properties for a thin convex lens. Calculate the image distance by dividing the product of the focal length and the object distance by the difference between the object distance and the focal length. Calculate the magnification by dividing the negative image distance by the object distance. Calculate the image height by multiplying the magnification by the object height. Check if the image is real by testing if the image distance is greater than zero. Check if the image is upright by testing if the magnification is greater than zero. Return a list containing the image distance, magnification, image height, real boolean, and upright boolean. Example 10, 15, 5 gives 30, -2, -10, true, false.

title: Solid Thermal Expansion
spec: Develop a function `expansion(length, alpha, initial, final)` to calculate the expansion of a solid rod. Calculate the temperature change by subtracting the initial temperature from the final temperature. Calculate the linear expansion amount by multiplying the length, the alpha coefficient, and the temperature change. Calculate the new length by adding the expansion amount to the original length. Calculate the percentage change by dividing the expansion amount by the original length and multiplying by one hundred. Determine if it is a contraction by checking if the temperature change is less than zero. Return the new length, percentage change, and contraction boolean. Example 100, 0.000012, 20, 70 yields 100.06, 0.06, false.

title: Roller Coaster Energy and Speed
spec: Provide `coaster(mass, height, friction, loop)` to analyze a roller coaster car dropping from a height. Calculate the initial potential energy by multiplying mass, a gravity constant of nine point eight, and height. Calculate energy lost to friction by multiplying the initial energy by the friction percentage divided by one hundred. Calculate the remaining kinetic energy by subtracting the lost energy from the initial energy. Calculate the velocity at the bottom by taking the square root of the quotient of twice the kinetic energy divided by the mass. Check if the velocity is sufficient to clear a loop by comparing if the velocity is greater than or equal to the loop threshold parameter. Return the velocity and the clearance boolean. Example 500, 50, 10, 25 yields 29.69, true.

title: Exercise Calorie and Deficit Calculator
spec: Write `calories(weight, height, age, met, minutes)` to estimate resting and active energy expenditure. Calculate the resting metabolic rate by multiplying weight by ten, adding height multiplied by six point two five, subtracting age multiplied by five, and adding five. Calculate the resting calories per minute by dividing the resting rate by fourteen hundred and forty. Calculate the active calories burned by multiplying the metabolic equivalent value, the weight in kilograms, and the minutes, then dividing by sixty. Calculate the total calories for the workout period by adding the active calories to the resting calories per minute multiplied by the minutes. If the total calories is greater than five hundred, classify as a high intensity workout. Return the resting rate, total workout calories, and the classification boolean. Example 80, 180, 30, 8, 45 gives 1780, 535.6, true.

title: Vehicle Fuel Economy Converter
spec: Implement a function `efficiency(mpg, price, distance)` to convert miles per gallon to metric and estimate trip costs. Calculate the liters per hundred kilometers by dividing two hundred and thirty five point two by the mpg. Calculate the total gallons needed for the trip by dividing the distance in miles by the mpg. Calculate the trip cost by multiplying the total gallons by the price per gallon. Calculate the cost per mile by dividing the trip cost by the distance. Check if the vehicle is highly efficient by determining if the mpg is greater than thirty five. Return a list of metric efficiency, trip cost, cost per mile, and the highly efficient boolean. Example 30, 3.50, 150 yields 7.84, 17.50, 0.116, false.

title: Baking Recipe Sugar Scaler
spec: Create a function `sugar(flour, original, target, liquid)` to adjust a baking recipe when reducing sugar. Calculate the sugar reduction percentage by subtracting the target from the original, dividing by the original, and multiplying by one hundred. Calculate the lost volume in cups by dividing the difference between the original and target sugar by two hundred. Calculate the new liquid amount by adding the lost volume multiplied by zero point five to the original liquid. Determine if a texture change is likely by checking if the reduction percentage is greater than twenty five. Return the new liquid amount, the reduction percentage, and the texture change boolean. Example 300, 200, 100, 100 yields 100.25, 50, true.

title: Submarine Buoyancy Adjuster
spec: Write `submarine(mass, volume, density, target)` to calculate the ballast water needed to reach a target depth buoyancy. Calculate the buoyant force by multiplying the submarine volume, the water density, and a gravity constant of nine point eight. Calculate the current weight by multiplying the mass by gravity. Calculate the net force by subtracting the current weight from the buoyant force. Calculate the required ballast mass by dividing the net force by gravity. Calculate the required ballast volume by dividing the required mass by the water density. Check if the required ballast is greater than the target ballast tank capacity. Return the net force, required ballast volume, and the capacity exceeded boolean. Example 5000, 6, 1025, 2 yields 11270, 1.12, false.

title: Heat Pump Efficiency and Payback
spec: Develop a function `geothermal(output, input, cost, electric)` to evaluate a heat pump system. Calculate the coefficient of performance by dividing the heat output by the electrical input. Calculate the daily running cost by multiplying the input by twenty four and then by the electric rate. Calculate the daily traditional cost by dividing the output by zero point nine, multiplying by twenty four, and then by the electric rate. Calculate the daily savings by subtracting the running cost from the traditional cost. Calculate the payback period in years by dividing the installation cost by the daily savings multiplied by three hundred and sixty five. Return true if the payback is less than ten years, else false, along with the coefficient and payback period. Example 10, 2, 15000, 0.15 gives true, 5, 1.25.

title: Storm Distance and Danger Estimator
spec: Write `lightning(seconds, temperature, shelter, thunder)` where shelter is a numerical distance to safety. Calculate the speed of sound in meters per second by multiplying the temperature in celsius by zero point six and adding three hundred and thirty one point three. Calculate the distance to the strike in meters by multiplying the speed of sound by the seconds elapsed. Calculate the time to reach safety by dividing the shelter distance by a running speed of five. A situation is dangerous if the distance is less than five thousand and the time to safety is greater than thirty. Return the speed of sound, the distance, the time to safety, and the danger boolean. Example 10, 20, 200, 120 yields 343.3, 3433, 40, true.

title: Bicycle Wheel Spoke Length
spec: Provide `spokes(rim, flange, offset, cross)` to compute the required spoke length for building a bicycle wheel. Calculate the radius of the rim by dividing it by two. Calculate the radius of the flange by dividing it by two. Calculate the cross angle in radians by multiplying the cross number by three hundred and sixty, dividing by thirty two, and multiplying by pi over one hundred and eighty. Calculate the squared terms by adding the square of the rim radius to the square of the flange radius, and adding the square of the offset. Calculate the length by taking the square root of the squared terms minus twice the rim radius times the flange radius times the cosine of the angle. If the offset is greater than zero, it is an asymmetric build. Return the cross angle, length, and a boolean for asymmetric. Example 600, 50, 5, 3 yields 0.589, 279.6, true.

title: Coffee Roasting Curve Analysis
spec: Implement `roast(start, crack, end, temperature)` to analyze a coffee roasting session. Calculate the total roast time by subtracting the start time from the end time. Calculate the development time by subtracting the crack time from the end time. Calculate the development ratio by dividing the development time by the total time, then multiplying by one hundred. Calculate the rate of rise by dividing the temperature by the crack time minus the start time. An ideal roast has a development ratio greater than or equal to twenty and less than or equal to twenty five. Return the total time, development ratio, rate of rise, and a boolean for ideal roast. Example 0, 8, 10, 400 yields 10, 20, 50, true.

title: Skydiver Terminal Velocity
spec: Write a function `parachute(mass, area, density, drag)` to estimate the terminal velocity of a skydiver. Calculate the skydiver weight by multiplying the mass by a gravity constant of nine point eight one. Calculate the drag denominator by multiplying the air density, the cross sectional area, and the drag coefficient. Calculate the terminal velocity by taking the square root of twice the weight divided by the drag denominator. Calculate the impact energy by multiplying zero point five by the mass and by the square of the terminal velocity. Determine if it is a safe landing by checking if the terminal velocity is less than or equal to six. Return the terminal velocity, impact energy, and the safe landing boolean. Example 80, 45, 1.225, 1.5 yields 4.35, 759.5, true.

title: Boiling Point Elevation Formula
spec: Create `boiling(elevation, mass, volume, constant)` to determine the boiling point of a saltwater solution at altitude. Calculate the atmospheric pressure drop by multiplying the elevation in meters by zero point zero zero one two. Calculate the baseline boiling point in celsius by subtracting the pressure drop from one hundred. Calculate the molality by dividing the solute mass in grams by fifty eight point four four, and then dividing by the solvent volume in liters. Calculate the boiling point elevation by multiplying the ebullioscopic constant by the molality and by a van t hoff factor of two. Calculate the final boiling point by adding the elevation to the baseline. Return the baseline, molality, and final boiling point. If the final boiling point is less than one hundred return true for lower otherwise false. Example 1000, 100, 2, 0.512 yields 98.8, 0.85, 99.67, true.

title: Paintball Drop Predictor
spec: Develop `paintball(velocity, angle, distance)` to model the drop of a fired paintball. Calculate the angle in radians by multiplying the angle in degrees by pi divided by one hundred and eighty. Calculate the horizontal velocity by multiplying the total velocity by the cosine of the angle. Calculate the time of flight by dividing the distance by the horizontal velocity. Calculate the initial vertical velocity by multiplying the total velocity by the sine of the angle. Calculate the vertical drop by multiplying the vertical velocity by the time of flight, then subtracting one half times nine point eight times the square of the time of flight. If the vertical drop is less than zero, return true for ground hit, otherwise false. Return the time of flight, vertical drop, and the boolean. Example 85, 5, 30 yields 0.35, 2.0, false.

title: Homebrew Beer Bitterness
spec: Provide a function `bitterness(ounces, alpha, volume, gravity)` to estimate the international bitterness units of a beer. Calculate the bigness factor by subtracting one from the gravity, multiplying by ten, and subtracting that from one point six five. Calculate the boil time factor by dividing the boil time of sixty by two hundred and eighty. Calculate the utilization by multiplying the bigness factor by the boil time factor. Calculate the international bitterness units by multiplying the ounces, the alpha acid percentage, the utilization, and seventy five, then dividing by the volume in gallons. If the units are greater than forty, return true for hoppy, otherwise false. Return the bigness factor, the bitterness units, and the hoppy boolean. Example 2, 5, 5, 1.050 yields 1.15, 36.9, false.

title: Simply Supported Bridge Load
spec: Write `bridge(span, load, position, capacity)` to calculate reactions and bending moments for a point load on a bridge. Calculate the distance from the right support by subtracting the load position from the span. Calculate the left reaction force by multiplying the load by the right distance and dividing by the span. Calculate the right reaction force by multiplying the load by the position and dividing by the span. Calculate the maximum bending moment by multiplying the load, the position, and the right distance, then dividing by the span. Determine if the bridge is safe by checking if the maximum moment is less than or equal to the structural capacity. Return the left reaction, right reaction, maximum moment, and safe boolean. Example 20, 5000, 5, 100000 yields 3750, 1250, 18750, true.

title: Ski Jumping Flight Distance
spec: Create `skijump(speed, angle, wind, mass)` to estimate the landing distance of a ski jumper. Calculate the takeoff vertical velocity by multiplying the speed by the sine of the angle in radians. Calculate the horizontal velocity by multiplying the speed by the cosine of the angle in radians. Calculate the air time by multiplying the vertical velocity by two and dividing by nine point eight. Calculate the base distance by multiplying the horizontal velocity by the air time. Calculate the wind effect by multiplying the wind speed by the air time and dividing by the mass. Calculate the final distance by adding the wind effect to the base distance. If the final distance is greater than one hundred, return true for a large hill rating, otherwise false. Return the air time, base distance, final distance, and the rating boolean. Example 25, 0.19, -2, 60 yields 0.96, 23.5, 23.47, false.

title: Aircraft Glide Distance Estimator
spec: Implement `glide(altitude, ratio, distance, wind, speed)` to determine if an airplane can glide to a runway after engine failure. Calculate the altitude in miles by dividing the altitude in feet by five thousand two hundred and eighty. Calculate the base glide distance in miles by multiplying the altitude in miles by the glide ratio. Calculate the time to descend in hours by dividing the base glide distance by the airspeed. Calculate the wind distance penalty by multiplying the headwind component by the time to descend. Calculate the actual glide distance by subtracting the wind distance penalty from the base glide distance. If the actual distance is greater than or equal to the distance to the runway, return true for reachable, otherwise false. Return the actual glide distance and the reachable boolean. Example 10560, 9, 15, 20, 100 yields 14.4, false.

title: Lawn Mowing Time Calculator
spec: Develop a function `mowing(length, width, deck, speed, battery)` to calculate the time required to mow a rectangular lawn. Calculate the effective cutting width by subtracting two inches of overlap from the deck width, then dividing by twelve to get feet. Calculate the area of the lawn by multiplying the length and the width. Calculate the total walking distance in feet by dividing the area by the effective cutting width. Calculate the total time in minutes by dividing the distance by the walking speed in feet per minute. Check if the job can be completed on one charge by comparing if the total time is less than or equal to the battery duration. Return the effective width, total distance, total time, and the one charge boolean. Example 100, 50, 22, 150, 45 yields 1.66, 3012, 20.08, true.

title: Trip Carbon Footprint
spec: Write a function `footprint(distance, efficiency)` that takes the total miles of a trip and the vehicle efficiency in miles per gallon.
