Calculate the total gallons of fuel consumed, and then multiply by twenty to find the total carbon dioxide in pounds. If the total carbon dioxide is greater than one thousand pounds, add a five percent penalty to it for long trip inefficiency. Calculate the number of trees needed to offset this carbon, assuming one tree absorbs forty pounds per year. Return a list containing the total carbon dioxide, the tree offset, and a boolean that is true if a penalty was applied. Example: providing 2000 and 25 returns [1680.0, 42.0, true].

title: Video File Size
spec: Write a function `filesize(duration, bitrate, audio)` that takes the video duration in seconds, the video bitrate in kilobits per second, and the audio bitrate in kilobits per second. Calculate the total kilobits for video and total kilobits for audio, then sum them to get the combined kilobits. Convert the combined kilobits to megabytes by dividing by eight thousand. If the resulting size is over five hundred megabytes, apply a ten percent compression reduction to the final megabytes. Return a list containing the final megabytes, the video megabytes before compression, and the audio megabytes before compression. Example: providing 600, 4000, and 128 returns [309.6, 300.0, 9.6].

title: Cloud Storage Biller
spec: Write a function `bill(gigabytes, retrievals)` that takes the monthly stored data in gigabytes and the number of data retrieval requests. The base cost is two cents per gigabyte, but if the stored data exceeds fifty gigabytes, the base cost for the entire storage is reduced to one point five cents per gigabyte. Retrievals cost zero point zero five cents each. Calculate the storage cost and the retrieval cost, then add them together for the subtotal. If the subtotal is less than a minimum fee of five dollars, set the final cost to five dollars. Return a list of the storage cost, retrieval cost, and final billed amount. Example: providing 10 and 1000 returns [0.2, 0.5, 5.0].

title: Parcel Volume Optimizer
spec: Write a function `parcel(length, width, height)` that takes the three dimensions of an item in inches. Calculate the base volume of the item, then add two inches of padding to each dimension to compute the new padded volume. The required box volume is the padded volume multiplied by a void fill factor of one point two. If the required box volume exceeds one thousand cubic inches, an oversize surcharge of five dollars is flagged. Return a list containing the original volume, the required box volume, and the surcharge amount which is zero if not oversize. Example: providing 10, 8, and 5 returns [400, 1008.0, 5].

title: Hydro Dam Output
spec: Write a function `power(head, flow, efficiency)` that takes the water head in meters, the flow rate in cubic meters per second, and the turbine efficiency as a decimal. Calculate the total available power in watts by multiplying water density of one thousand, gravity of nine point eight, head, and flow. Multiply this available power by the efficiency to get the generated electrical power in watts, then convert to megawatts by dividing by one million. If the output falls below ten megawatts, flag the operation as low output. Return a list of the total available megawatts, generated megawatts, and a boolean for low output. Example: providing 50, 20, and 0.9 returns [9.8, 8.82, true].

title: Elevator Boarding Wait
spec: Write a function `boarding(people, capacity, time)` that takes the number of people waiting, the elevator passenger capacity, and the round trip time in seconds. Calculate the number of full trips required by dividing the people by the capacity and rounding down. Calculate the remaining people that will board on the final trip. The total wait time for the last person is the number of full trips multiplied by the round trip time. If the remaining people is greater than zero, an extra trip is needed, but the last person's wait time does not include this final return trip. If the wait time exceeds three hundred seconds, flag the lobby as congested. Return a list of the full trips, the wait time for the last person, and the congested boolean. Example: providing 45, 10, and 60 returns [4, 240.0, false].

title: Canine Feeding Ration
spec: Write a function `ration(weight, age, activity)` that takes the dog weight in kilograms, age in years, and an activity multiplier. Calculate the resting energy requirement by multiplying the weight by thirty and adding seventy. The daily calorie need is the resting energy requirement multiplied by the activity multiplier. If the age is less than one year, add a puppy growth premium of two hundred calories to the daily need. A standard cup of dog food contains three hundred and thirty five calories. Calculate the required cups of food by dividing the final daily calorie need by three hundred and thirty five. Return a list of the resting energy, total calories, and cups of food. Example: providing 20, 3, and 1.5 returns [670.0, 1005.0, 3.0].

title: Server Rack Heatflow
spec: Write a function `heatflow(servers, watts, airflow)` that takes the number of servers, the power consumption per server in watts, and the rack airflow in cubic feet per minute. The total power is the number of servers multiplied by the watts. Practically all power consumed is converted to heat, so the total heat load is the total power multiplied by three point four one to get british thermal units per hour. The expected temperature rise in degrees fahrenheit is the total heat load divided by the product of the airflow and one point zero eight. If the temperature rise is above twenty degrees, flag the rack as overheating. Return a list of the total power, temperature rise, and overheating boolean. Example: providing 10, 270, and 500 returns [2700.0, 17.05, false].

title: Lye Saponification Value
spec: Write a function `saponification(olive, coconut, lye)` that takes the mass of olive oil in grams, coconut oil in grams, and the standard lye concentration percentage as a decimal. The saponification value for olive oil is zero point one three four and for coconut oil is zero point one nine. Calculate the required lye for olive oil by multiplying its mass by its saponification value. Calculate the required lye for coconut oil by multiplying its mass by its saponification value. Sum these to get the total required lye. The total water needed is the total required lye divided by the lye concentration, minus the total required lye. Return a list of the olive lye, coconut lye, and total water needed. Example: providing 500, 200, and 0.3 returns [67.0, 38.0, 245.0].

title: Leaf Transpiration Rate
spec: Write a function `transpiration(temperature, humidity, wind)` that takes the ambient temperature in celsius, the relative humidity percentage, and the wind speed in meters per second. The base evaporation rate is the temperature multiplied by zero point two. Subtract the humidity multiplied by zero point zero five from the base rate, then add the wind speed multiplied by zero point one. If the resulting rate is negative, set it to zero. A rate greater than four is considered high stress for the plant. Return a list containing the calculated rate and a boolean indicating if the plant is under high stress. Example: providing 30, 40, and 5 returns [4.5, true].

title: Gratuity Pool Share
spec: Write a function `gratuity(hours, tips, points)` that takes a worker's hours for the shift, the total tips collected by the entire staff, and a multiplier based on the worker's role. The total points for the worker is their hours multiplied by their role multiplier. Assume the entire staff accumulated a fixed sum of one hundred total points for the shift, making the point value the total tips divided by one hundred. The worker's share is their total points multiplied by the point value. If their share divided by their hours is less than two dollars per hour, an additional top up of ten dollars is awarded. Return a list of the worker's total points, their base tip share, and their final tip amount including any top up. Example: providing 8, 500, and 1.5 returns [12.0, 60.0, 60.0].

title: Bungee Cord Dynamics
spec: Write a function `bungee(mass, length, stiffness)` that takes the jumper mass in kilograms, the unstretched cord length in meters, and the cord stiffness in newtons per meter. The static stretch is the mass multiplied by gravity of nine point eight, divided by the stiffness. The maximum dynamic stretch is double the static stretch, and the total fall distance is the cord length plus the dynamic stretch. The peak force experienced by the jumper is the dynamic stretch multiplied by the stiffness. If the peak force exceeds two thousand newtons, the jump is considered extreme. Return a list of the dynamic stretch, total fall distance, peak force, and the extreme boolean. Example: providing 75, 20, and 200 returns [7.35, 27.35, 1470.0, false].

title: Escalator Throughput
spec: Write a function `escalator(speed, steps, occupancy)` that takes the escalator speed in steps per second, the total visible steps, and the average passenger occupancy per step. Calculate the maximum theoretical passengers per minute by multiplying speed, sixty seconds, and a maximum occupancy of two. Calculate the actual passengers per minute by multiplying speed, sixty seconds, and the given average occupancy. The journey time in seconds is the total visible steps divided by the speed. If the actual passengers per minute is less than fifty percent of the maximum theoretical throughput, flag the escalator as underutilized. Return a list containing the journey time, actual passengers per minute, and the underutilized boolean. Example: providing 2, 60, and 0.8 returns [30.0, 96.0, true].

title: Typing Test Metrics
spec: Write a function `typing(characters, time, errors)` that takes the total characters typed, the time taken in seconds, and the number of uncorrected errors. Calculate the gross words per minute by dividing the characters by five, then multiplying by sixty and dividing by the time. Calculate the error penalty by multiplying the errors by two. The net words per minute is the gross words per minute minus the error penalty, but if it is negative, set it to zero. The accuracy percentage is the characters minus the errors, divided by the characters, multiplied by one hundred. Return a list of the gross words per minute, net words per minute, and accuracy percentage. Example: providing 300, 60, and 3 returns [60.0, 54.0, 99.0].

title: Press Ink Usage
spec: Write a function `ink(pages, coverage, colors)` that takes the total number of printed pages, the ink coverage percentage per page as a decimal, and the number of distinct color plates used. One milliliter of ink covers a standard page at five percent coverage, so calculate the required ink per page in milliliters by dividing the coverage by zero point zero five. The raw ink volume is the required ink per page multiplied by the number of pages. For each color plate beyond the first, add a flat waste penalty of fifty milliliters for press setup to get the total ink required. If the total ink exceeds one thousand milliliters, flag the job for a bulk ink order. Return a list of the raw ink volume, total ink required, and the bulk order boolean. Example: providing 500, 0.10, and 4 returns [1000.0, 1150.0, true].

title: Intersection Light Timing
spec: Write a function `timing(speed, width, perception)` that takes the approach speed limit in meters per second, the intersection width in meters, and a driver perception time in seconds. A vehicle's deceleration rate is assumed to be three meters per square second. Calculate the minimum yellow light time by adding the perception time to the result of dividing the speed by double the deceleration rate. Calculate the red clearance time by dividing the intersection width by the speed. The total phase time is the yellow light time plus the red clearance time, and if it is less than four seconds, set it to a minimum of four seconds. Return a list of the yellow light time, red clearance time, and total phase time. Example: providing 12, 24, and 1.0 returns [3.0, 2.0, 5.0].

title: Runway Takeoff Distance
spec: Write a function `takeoff(weight, thrust, drag)` that takes the aircraft takeoff weight in kilograms, the total engine thrust in newtons, and a combined aerodynamic and friction drag factor. The net accelerating force is the thrust minus the product of weight, gravity of nine point eight, and the drag factor. Calculate the acceleration by dividing the net force by the weight. The required takeoff speed is sixty meters per second. The takeoff distance is the square of the takeoff speed divided by twice the acceleration. If the distance exceeds two thousand meters, flag the runway as insufficient for a standard departure. Return a list of the net force, takeoff distance, and the insufficient boolean. Example: providing 50000, 150000, and 0.05 returns [125500.0, 717.13, false].

title: Ticketing Revenue Projection
spec: Write a function `ticketing(capacity, price, sold)` that takes the maximum seating capacity, the base ticket price, and the total tickets sold. Twenty percent of the sold tickets are VIP tickets with a fifty percent price premium, while the rest are sold at the base price. Calculate the number of VIP tickets and standard tickets sold, then compute their respective revenues. The total revenue is the sum of VIP revenue and standard revenue. The occupancy rate is the total tickets sold divided by the maximum capacity, and if it is below zero point six, flag the event as underperforming. Return a list of the total revenue, occupancy rate, and underperforming boolean. Example: providing 1000, 50, and 800 returns [44000.0, 0.8, false].

title: Rainwater Runoff Catchment
spec: Write a function `catchment(area, rainfall, efficiency)` that takes the roof catchment area in square meters, the annual rainfall in millimeters, and the runoff efficiency factor. The total rainfall volume in liters is the area multiplied by the rainfall, and the collectable water is this volume multiplied by the efficiency factor. During the first flush of rain, five percent of the collectable water is diverted to clear debris. The final usable water is the collectable water minus the first flush diversion. A standard storage tank holds five thousand liters, so calculate how many full tanks are needed to store the usable water by dividing the final usable water by five thousand and rounding down. Return a list of the collectable water, the final usable water, and the number of full tanks. Example: providing 150, 600, and 0.8 returns [72000.0, 68400.0, 13].

title: Snowplow Route Time
spec: Write a function `plowing(distance, speed, depth)` that takes the route distance in kilometers, the base plowing speed in kilometers per hour, and the snow depth in centimeters. For every centimeter of snow depth above five centimeters, the base speed is reduced by zero point five kilometers per hour. If the adjusted speed falls below ten kilometers per hour, set it to ten kilometers per hour. The clearing time in hours is the route distance divided by the adjusted speed. The truck consumes diesel at a rate of thirty liters per hour, so calculate the total fuel used by multiplying the clearing time by thirty. Return a list containing the adjusted speed, clearing time, and total fuel used. Example: providing 60, 40, and 25 returns [30.0, 2.0, 60.0].

title: Geothermal Loop Sizing
spec: Write a function `geothermal(load, conductivity, depth)` that takes the building heating load in watts, the soil thermal conductivity in watts per meter-kelvin, and the installation depth in meters. The base required pipe length is the heating load divided by the soil conductivity. The temperature of the ground increases slightly with depth, so for every meter of depth beyond two meters, reduce the base pipe length by one percent, up to a maximum reduction of twenty percent. Calculate the percentage reduction and apply it to the base length to get the final loop length. If the final length is greater than five hundred meters, two parallel loops must be installed. Return a list of the base length, final length, and a boolean indicating if two loops are needed. Example: providing 12000, 1.5, and 12 returns [8000.0, 7200.0, true].

title: Spool Filament Usage
spec: Write a function `filament(perimeters, infill, height)` that takes the length of perimeter lines in millimeters, the length of infill lines in millimeters, and the layer height in millimeters. The total extruded line length is the sum of perimeters and infill. The volume of plastic extruded per millimeter of line is the layer height multiplied by an extrusion width of zero point four. Calculate the total volume of plastic in cubic millimeters by multiplying the total line length by the volume per millimeter. The mass of the print in grams is the total volume multiplied by a plastic density of zero point zero zero one two five grams per cubic millimeter. If the mass exceeds one thousand grams, flag the print as requiring a new large spool. Return a list of the total line length, total mass, and the large spool boolean. Example: providing 50000, 150000, and 0.2 returns [200000.0, 20.0, false].

title: Snowmaking Water Demand
spec: Write a function `snowmaking(area, depth, density)` that takes the trail area in square meters, the target snow depth in meters, and the snow density in kilograms per cubic meter. The total snow volume is the area multiplied by the depth. Calculate the mass of the snow by multiplying the volume by the density. Water has a density of one thousand kilograms per cubic meter. Calculate the total cubic meters of water required by dividing the snow mass by one thousand. A standard snow gun can process five cubic meters of water per hour. Calculate the hours required for a single gun to produce the snow. Return a list of the snow volume, water volume, and single gun hours. Example: providing 10000, 0.5, and 400 returns [5000.0, 2000.0, 400.0].

title: Tower Crane Moment
spec: Write a function `crane(load, distance, counterweight)` that takes the lifted load in kilograms, the distance from the mast in meters, and the mass of the counterweight in kilograms. The load moment is the lifted load multiplied by the distance. The counterweight moment is the counterweight mass multiplied by a fixed distance of fifteen meters. The net moment on the mast is the absolute difference between the load moment and the counterweight moment. If the net moment exceeds fifty thousand kilogram-meters, the crane is overloaded. Return a list containing the load moment, counterweight moment, net moment, and a boolean indicating if it is overloaded. Example: providing 2000, 30, and 4000 returns [60000.0, 60000.0, 0.0, false].

title: Loom Yarn Requirement
spec: Write a function `weaving(width, length, density)` that takes the fabric width in centimeters, fabric length in centimeters, and thread density in threads per centimeter. The number of warp threads running lengthwise is the width multiplied by the density, and the total warp yarn length in meters is the number of warp threads multiplied by the fabric length divided by one hundred. The number of weft threads running crosswise is the length multiplied by the density, and the total weft yarn length in meters is the number of weft threads multiplied by the fabric width divided by one hundred. To account for loom waste, add ten percent to both the total warp length and total weft length. Return a list of the total warp length, total weft length, and the combined grand total yarn length in meters. Example: providing 100, 200, and 10 returns [2200.0, 2200.0, 4400.0].

title: Centrifugal Pump Head
spec: Write `analyze(system)` to calculate the total dynamic head of a water pump. The input is a list containing static lift in meters, pipe length in meters, pipe diameter in meters, friction factor, and volumetric flow rate. First, calculate the fluid velocity by dividing the flow rate by the pipe cross sectional area, assuming pi is 3.14. Next, calculate the friction head by multiplying the friction factor, pipe length, and the square of velocity, then dividing by the product of the diameter, 2.0, and gravity at 9.81. Add the friction head to the static lift to get the total head. Finally, calculate the hydraulic power by multiplying the total head, flow rate, fluid density at 1000.0, and gravity. Return a tuple of velocity, total head, and hydraulic power. Example: input [10.0, 50.0, 0.2, 0.02, 0.1] returns (3.18, 10.51, 10310.3).

title: Medical Oxygen Duration
spec: Implement `evaluate(tank)` to assess breathable time for a patient. The input is a list containing cylinder physical volume in liters, current pressure in atm, patient flow rate in liters per minute, safety reserve pressure, empty tank mass in kg, and oxygen density. Calculate total available liters by multiplying volume and current pressure. Calculate the safety volume by multiplying the physical volume and safety reserve pressure. Determine the usable gas mass by multiplying the difference between total and safety volumes by the density. Calculate the remaining usable liters and divide by the flow rate to find available minutes. Return a tuple of usable liters, available minutes, current total mass, and a boolean that is true if available minutes are below 30. Example: input [10.0, 150.0, 2.0, 20.0, 14.0, 0.0013] returns (1300.0, 650.0, 15.69, False).

title: Capacitor Discharge Timing
spec: Create `discharge(circuit)` to analyze an electronic circuit. The input is a list of capacitance in farads, resistance in ohms, initial voltage, and target voltage. Calculate the time constant by multiplying the resistance and capacitance. Calculate the initial stored energy by multiplying 0.5, the capacitance, and the initial voltage squared. Calculate the final stored energy using the target voltage instead. Find the energy dissipated by subtracting the final energy from the initial energy. Estimate the time to reach the target voltage by multiplying the time constant by the natural logarithm of the initial voltage divided by the target voltage. Return a tuple of the time constant, time to target, and energy dissipated. Example: input [0.001, 1000.0, 12.0, 3.0] returns (1.0, 1.38, 0.0675).

title: Conveyor Belt Tension
spec: Write `calculate(conveyor)` to evaluate a material transport system. The input is a list of mass per meter of material, belt length, incline angle in radians, friction coefficient, and belt speed. Calculate the total material mass by multiplying mass per meter and length. Calculate the friction force by multiplying the total mass, gravity at 9.8, the friction coefficient, and the cosine of the angle. Calculate the incline force by multiplying the total mass, gravity, and the sine of the angle. Add the friction and incline forces to find the total belt tension. Multiply the total tension by the belt speed to find the required motor power. Return a tuple of total mass, total tension, and motor power. Example: input [20.0, 50.0, 0.2, 0.05, 2.0] returns (1000.0, 2439.4, 4878.8).

title: Sediment Settling Velocity
spec: Implement `settling(particle)` to evaluate water treatment. The input is a list of particle diameter in meters, particle density, water density, water viscosity, and tank depth. Calculate the net density difference by subtracting water density from particle density. Calculate the settling velocity using Stokes law by multiplying gravity at 9.81, the density difference, and the square of the diameter, then dividing by the product of 18 and the viscosity. Calculate the time to settle by dividing the tank depth by the settling velocity. Return a tuple of the density difference, settling velocity, time to settle, and a boolean that is true if the settling time is less than 7200 seconds. Example: input [0.0001, 2650.0, 1000.0, 0.001, 2.0] returns (1650.0, 0.0089, 222.4, True).

title: Sailboat Mast Load
spec: Write `analyze(rigging)` to determine forces on a sailing vessel. The input is a list of wind force in newtons, sail center of effort height in meters, shroud base width in meters, mast weight, and hull righting moment. Calculate the heeling moment by multiplying the wind force and the center of effort height. Check if the heeling moment is greater than the hull righting moment and set a warning flag. Calculate the shroud tension by dividing the heeling moment by the shroud base width. Calculate the mast compression by multiplying the shroud tension by the sail height and dividing by the shroud base width, then adding the mast weight. Return a tuple of heeling moment, shroud tension, mast compression, and the warning flag. Example: input [2000.0, 5.0, 2.0, 500.0, 12000.0] returns (10000.0, 5000.0, 13000.0, False).

title: Distillation Reflux Ratio
spec: Develop `simulate(column)` to evaluate a chemical separation process. The input is a list of feed flow rate, distillate flow rate, molar reflux ratio, feed concentration, and distillate concentration. Calculate the bottom product flow rate by subtracting the distillate flow rate from the feed flow rate. Calculate the liquid returned to the column by multiplying the distillate rate by the reflux ratio. Calculate the total vapor flow leaving the top by adding the liquid returned and the distillate rate. Find the bottoms concentration by subtracting the product of distillate rate and concentration from the product of feed rate and concentration, then dividing by the bottom product flow rate. Return a tuple of the bottoms flow rate, total vapor flow, and bottoms concentration. Example: input [100.0, 40.0, 2.5, 0.5, 0.95] returns (60.0, 140.0, 0.2).

title: Blood Pressure Metrics
spec: Implement `assess(vitals)` to evaluate a patient circulatory health. The input is a list of systolic pressure, diastolic pressure, heart rate, and patient age. Calculate the pulse pressure by subtracting diastolic from systolic. Calculate the mean arterial pressure by adding the diastolic pressure and one third of the pulse pressure. Estimate the stroke volume proxy by multiplying the pulse pressure by 2.0. Calculate the cardiac output proxy by multiplying the stroke volume proxy by the heart rate and dividing by 1000.0. Determine if the patient is hypertensive by checking if systolic is above 130.0 or diastolic is above 80.0. Return a tuple of the pulse pressure, mean arterial pressure, cardiac output proxy, and the hypertensive status. Example: input [120.0, 80.0, 70.0, 45.0] returns (40.0, 93.33, 5.6, False).

title: Traffic Flow Speed
spec: Write `evaluate(traffic)` to analyze highway congestion. The input is a list of observed flow rate in cars per hour, jam density in cars per mile, free flow speed in miles per hour, and a lane count. Calculate the capacity per lane by multiplying the free flow speed and jam density, then dividing by 4.0. Calculate total capacity by multiplying lane count and capacity per lane. Calculate the current density per lane by dividing the observed flow rate by the lane count and then by the free flow speed. If current density exceeds jam density divided by 2.0, set a congested flag to true. Estimate average speed by subtracting the product of free flow speed and current density divided by jam density from the free flow speed. Return a tuple of total capacity, average speed, and the congested flag. Example: input [3000.0, 120.0, 60.0, 2.0] returns (3600.0, 47.5, False).

title: Cable Car Sag
spec: Develop `deflection(cable)` to measure transport safety. The input is a list of span length in meters, cable tension in newtons, point load mass in kg, cable mass per unit length, and gravity. Calculate the distributed load sag by multiplying the cable mass, gravity, and the square of the span length, then dividing by the product of 8.0 and the cable tension. Calculate the point load sag by multiplying the point load mass, gravity, and the span length, then dividing by the product of 4.0 and the tension. Calculate the total sag by adding the distributed and point load sags. The system is unsafe if the total sag exceeds the span length divided by 20.0. Return a tuple of the distributed sag, point load sag, total sag, and a boolean for the safety status. Example: input [200.0, 50000.0, 800.0, 5.0, 9.8] returns (9.8, 7.84, 17.64, True).

title: Acoustic Reverberation
spec: Write `analyze(room)` to evaluate concert hall acoustics. The input is a list of room length, room width, room height, wall absorption coefficient, and floor absorption coefficient. Calculate the room volume by multiplying length, width, and height. Calculate the wall area by adding the product of length and height to the product of width and height, then multiplying by 2.0. Calculate the floor and ceiling area by multiplying length and width. Calculate total sound absorption by multiplying the wall area by its coefficient, adding the product of the floor area and its coefficient, and adding the product of the ceiling area and a fixed coefficient of 0.1. Calculate the reverberation time by multiplying 0.161 and the volume, then dividing by the total absorption. Return a tuple of volume, total absorption, and reverberation time. Example: input [20.0, 15.0, 5.0, 0.05, 0.2] returns (1500.0, 107.5, 2.24).

title: Thermal Bridging
spec: Implement `heat(wall)` to evaluate construction insulation. The input is a list of total wall area, stud width, stud spacing, cavity insulation resistance, and wood stud resistance. Calculate the framing fraction by dividing the stud width by the stud spacing. Calculate the cavity fraction by subtracting the framing fraction from 1.0. Calculate the overall wall conductance by adding the framing fraction divided by the stud resistance to the cavity fraction divided by the cavity insulation resistance. Calculate the effective resistance by taking the inverse of the overall conductance. Calculate the heat loss rate by dividing the total wall area by the effective resistance. Return a tuple of the framing fraction, effective resistance, and heat loss rate. Example: input [100.0, 0.05, 0.4, 3.5, 1.0] returns (0.125, 2.66, 37.5).

title: Electric Motor Torque
spec: Create `evaluate(motor)` to assess industrial equipment performance. The input is a list of applied voltage, drawn current, motor efficiency as a decimal, operating speed in revolutions per minute, and a maximum torque limit. Calculate the input electrical power by multiplying voltage and current. Calculate the output mechanical power by multiplying the electrical power and the efficiency. Calculate the angular velocity by multiplying the speed by 3.14159 and dividing by 30.0. Calculate the operating torque by dividing the mechanical power by the angular velocity. Evaluate a warning flag that is true if the operating torque is greater than or equal to the maximum torque limit. Return a tuple of the input power, operating torque, and the warning flag. Example: input [400.0, 20.0, 0.9, 1500.0, 50.0] returns (8000.0, 45.83, False).

title: Radioactive Decay
spec: Write `decay(sample)` to analyze isotope breakdown. The input is a list of initial mass in grams, half life in years, elapsed time in years, and atomic mass. Calculate the decay constant by dividing 0.693 by the half life. Calculate the remaining mass by multiplying the initial mass by the exponent of the negative decay constant times the elapsed time. Calculate the decayed mass by subtracting the remaining mass from the initial mass. Estimate the current activity in becquerels by multiplying the decay constant, the remaining mass, Avogadro's number of 6.022e23, and dividing by the atomic mass, then adjusting for years to seconds by dividing by 31536000.0. Return a tuple of the decay constant, remaining mass, and current activity. Example: input [10.0, 5.27, 10.0, 60.0] returns (0.131, 2.68, 1.1e15).

title: Greenhouse Heating
spec: Develop `climate(greenhouse)` to size a boiler for agriculture. The input is a list of roof area, wall area, roof heat transfer coefficient, wall heat transfer coefficient, target indoor temperature, and minimum outdoor temperature. Calculate the temperature difference by subtracting the outdoor temperature from the target temperature. Calculate the roof heat loss by multiplying the roof area, its transfer coefficient, and the temperature difference. Calculate the wall heat loss by multiplying the wall area, its transfer coefficient, and the temperature difference. Calculate the total heat loss by adding the roof and wall losses. Add a safety factor by multiplying the total heat loss by 1.2 to find the boiler capacity. Return a tuple of the temperature difference, total heat loss, and boiler capacity. Example: input [200.0, 150.0, 2.5, 1.5, 20.0, -5.0] returns (25.0, 18125.0, 21750.0).

title: Glacier Melt Rate
spec: Implement `ablation(glacier)` to estimate daily ice loss. The input is a list containing average air temperature in Celsius, incoming shortwave radiation, ice albedo fraction, and wind speed. Calculate the positive degree day melt by multiplying the temperature by 4.5 if the temperature is greater than 0.0, otherwise the melt is 0.0. Calculate the net shortwave radiation by multiplying the incoming radiation by the result of 1.0 minus the albedo fraction. Estimate the sensible heat flux by multiplying the temperature, the wind speed, and a transfer coefficient of 1.2. Calculate the total daily melt in millimeters by adding the degree day melt, the net radiation divided by 334.0, and the sensible heat flux. Return a tuple of the net radiation, sensible heat flux, and total melt. Example: input [5.0, 400.0, 0.4, 2.0] returns (240.0, 12.0, 35.2).

title: Gas Pipeline Flow
spec: Write `evaluate(pipeline)` to measure natural gas transport. The input is a list of upstream pressure, downstream pressure, pipe diameter, pipe length, and gas specific gravity. Calculate the pressure difference by subtracting the square of the downstream pressure from the square of the upstream pressure. Calculate the transmission factor by dividing 1.0 by the square root of the gas gravity. Estimate the flow rate by multiplying 0.0011, the transmission factor, the square root of the pressure difference divided by the length, and the pipe diameter raised to the power of 2.5. Calculate the average pressure by adding the upstream and downstream pressures and dividing by 2.0. Return a tuple of the pressure difference, flow rate, and average pressure. Example: input [100.0, 80.0, 0.5, 10.0, 0.6] returns (3600.0, 0.05, 90.0).

title: Dietary Fiber Energy
spec: Create `nutrition(meal)` to estimate actual caloric yield of fibers. The input is a list of grams of soluble fiber, grams of insoluble fiber, moisture fraction, and protein content. Calculate the fermentable mass by multiplying the soluble fiber by 0.8 and adding it to the insoluble fiber multiplied by 0.2. Calculate the short chain fatty acid yield by multiplying the fermentable mass by 0.6. Calculate the calories derived by multiplying the fatty acid yield by 2.4. Calculate the adjusted total dry mass by subtracting the product of the moisture fraction and the sum of all inputs from the sum of all inputs. Return a tuple of the fermentable mass, derived calories, and adjusted total mass. Example: input [10.0, 15.0, 0.1, 20.0] returns (11.0, 15.84, 40.5).

title: Photovoltaic Inverter
spec: Implement `clipping(array)` to assess solar energy losses. The input is a list of exactly three hourly solar irradiance values, followed by the array surface area, panel efficiency, and the inverter maximum power limit. Initialize total delivered and total clipped to zero. For each of the three irradiance values, calculate the potential power by multiplying the irradiance, area, and efficiency. If the potential power exceeds the inverter limit, add the inverter limit to delivered power and add the difference to clipped power. Otherwise, add the potential power to delivered power. Calculate the loss percentage by dividing the total clipped energy by the sum of delivered and clipped energy, then multiplying by 100.0. Return a tuple of total delivered, total clipped, and the loss percentage. Example: input [500.0, 1000.0, 200.0, 10.0, 0.2, 1500.0] returns (2900.0, 500.0, 14.7).

title: Furnace Efficiency
spec: Write `combustion(furnace)` to measure heating system performance. The input is a list of fuel mass burned per hour, fuel heating value, useful heat delivered, exhaust gas mass, and exhaust temperature. Calculate the total energy input by multiplying the fuel mass and the heating value. Calculate the sensible heat loss by multiplying the exhaust gas mass, a specific heat capacity of 1.04, and the difference between the exhaust temperature and a room temperature of 20.0. Calculate the combustion efficiency by dividing the useful heat by the total energy input. Calculate the unaccounted energy loss by subtracting the useful heat and the sensible heat loss from the total energy input. Return a tuple of the sensible heat loss, efficiency, and unaccounted loss. Example: input [10.0, 40000.0, 320000.0, 150.0, 200.0] returns (28080.0, 0.8, 51920.0).

title: Tidal Respiration
spec: Develop `ventilation(patient)` to assess lung function. The input is a list of tidal volume in milliliters, anatomic dead space in milliliters, and breathing frequency in breaths per minute. Calculate the minute ventilation by multiplying the tidal volume and the breathing frequency, then dividing by 1000.0 to convert to liters. Calculate the alveolar ventilation by subtracting the dead space from the tidal volume, multiplying by the breathing frequency, and dividing by 1000.0. Calculate the dead space ratio by dividing the dead space by the tidal volume. A warning flag is set to true if the alveolar ventilation is less than 4.0 or the dead space ratio is greater than 0.5. Return a tuple of minute ventilation, alveolar ventilation, dead space ratio, and the warning flag. Example: input [500.0, 150.0, 12.0] returns (6.0, 4.2, 0.3, False).

title: Wind Chill Time
spec: Implement `frostbite(weather)` to evaluate extreme cold exposure danger. The input is a list of air temperature in Celsius, wind speed in kilometers per hour, and exposed skin area. Calculate the wind chill index by adding 13.12 and 0.6215 times the temperature, subtracting 11.37 times the wind speed raised to 0.16, and adding 0.3965 times the temperature times the wind speed raised to 0.16. Estimate the heat loss rate by multiplying the skin area by the difference between a skin temperature of 33.0 and the wind chill index, then dividing by a thermal resistance of 0.1. Set a severe danger flag if the wind chill is below -27.0. Return a tuple of the wind chill index, heat loss rate, and the danger flag. Example: input [-10.0, 30.0, 0.5] returns (-20.1, 265.5, False).

title: Magnetic Field Strength
spec: Write `electromagnet(coil)` to analyze a solenoid. The input is a list of the number of wire turns, length of the solenoid in meters, current in amperes, and relative permeability of the core. Calculate the turn density by dividing the number of turns by the length. Calculate the magnetic field at the center by multiplying the relative permeability, the vacuum permeability of 0.000001256, the turn density, and the current. Calculate the magnetic flux by multiplying the field by a cross sectional area of 0.05. Set a saturation flag to true if the magnetic field is greater than 1.6. Return a tuple of the turn density, the magnetic field, the flux, and the saturation flag. Example: input [1000.0, 0.2, 5.0, 200.0] returns (5000.0, 6.28, 0.314, True).

title: Gearbox Ratio
spec: Create `transmission(gears)` to evaluate a mechanical drive. The input is a list of the number of teeth on the input gear, idler gear, and output gear, along with the input speed in rpm and input torque. Calculate the primary ratio by dividing the idler teeth by the input teeth. Calculate the secondary ratio by dividing the output teeth by the idler teeth. Calculate the total gear ratio by multiplying the primary and secondary ratios. Calculate the output speed by dividing the input speed by the total gear ratio. Calculate the ideal output torque by multiplying the input torque and the total gear ratio. Calculate the actual output torque by multiplying the ideal torque by an efficiency factor of 0.95. Return a tuple of the total ratio, output speed, and actual output torque. Example: input [20.0, 40.0, 60.0, 3000.0, 100.0] returns (3.0, 1000.0, 285.0).

title: Sedimentation Tank
spec: Develop `clarifier(tank)` to assess water purification. The input is a list of volumetric flow rate, tank width, tank length, tank water depth, and target particle settling velocity. Calculate the tank surface area by multiplying the width and the length. Calculate the tank volume by multiplying the surface area and the depth. Calculate the surface overflow rate by dividing the flow rate by the surface area. Calculate the hydraulic retention time by dividing the volume by the flow rate. Evaluate a success flag which is true if the target particle settling velocity is greater than the surface overflow rate and the retention time is greater than 120.0. Return a tuple of the surface area, retention time, overflow rate, and the success flag. Example: input [0.5, 10.0, 30.0, 4.0, 0.002] returns (300.0, 2400.0, 0.00167, True).

title: Commercial Laundry Sizing
spec: Write a function `sizing(rooms, occupancy)` that calculates laundry loads for a hotel. Total beds is rooms times occupancy. Sheets weight is total beds times three point five. Towels weight is total beds times two point two. If occupancy is greater than zero point eight, add ten percent to the towels weight for pool usage (multiply by one point one). Total weight is sheets weight plus towels weight. Wash cycles is total weight divided by fifty. If wash cycles is greater than ten, add five to the total weight to account for extra detergent processing. Return a tuple containing the wash cycles and the final total weight. Example: inputting 10 and 0.9 returns approximately 1.0656 and 53.28.

title: Wallpaper Material Estimator
spec: Create a function `wallpaper(perimeter, height, repeat)` to estimate wallpaper requirements. The number of drops needed is the perimeter divided by zero point five. The drop length is the height plus the pattern repeat plus zero point two for trimming. Total fabric is the drops multiplied by the drop length. A roll holds ten meters, so rolls needed is total fabric divided by ten. If rolls needed is less than three, add one to the rolls needed for safety. If the drop length is greater than three, subtract zero point five from the total fabric to account for bulk efficiency. Return the rolls needed and total fabric length. Example: inputs 10.0, 2.5, and 0.5 returns 6.4 and 63.5.

title: Bricklaying Mortar Estimator
spec: Write a function `mortar(length, height, thickness)` to calculate materials for a brick wall. Wall area is length times height. Bricks needed is the area times sixty. The base mortar required is bricks times zero point zero zero one. If the thickness is greater than one, multiply the base mortar by two. Add ten percent to the base mortar for waste (multiply by one point one). The sand volume is the final mortar times zero point seven five, and the cement volume is the final mortar times zero point two five. Return a tuple of bricks needed, sand volume, and cement volume. Example: inputs 10, 2, and 0.5 returns 1200, 0.99, and 0.33.

title: Motorcycle Chain Sizing
spec: Develop a function `chain(pitch, front, rear, distance)` to determine the correct chain length. Sprocket links are the front plus rear teeth divided by two. Chainstay in inches is the distance divided by pitch. Length links are the chainstay in inches times two. Total links is the sprocket links plus length links plus one. If total links is less than one hundred, add two links for suspension travel. If the rear teeth count is greater than forty, add one more link. Total length in inches is total links times the pitch. Return the total links and total length. Example: inputs 0.5, 15, 45, and 25.0 returns 132 and 66.0.

title: Aquarium Filtration Capacity
spec: Write a function `filtration(volume, bioload, planted)` to size an aquarium filter. The base turnover rate is volume times four. If the bioload is greater than five, add the volume times two to the turnover rate. If planted is exactly equal to one, subtract the volume from the turnover rate. The filter volume needed is the turnover rate divided by twenty. If the filter volume is less than two, set it to two. Media weight is the filter volume times zero point five. Return the turnover rate, filter volume, and media weight. Example: inputs 50.0, 6.0, and 1 returns 250.0, 12.5, and 6.25.

title: Tent Seating Capacity
spec: Create a function `seating(length, width, dancefloor)` to calculate event tables. Total area is length times width. Usable area is total area minus the dancefloor area. If usable area is less than fifty, return zero for both tables and chairs. Tables needed is usable area divided by eight. Total chairs is tables needed times ten. If the length is greater than the width times two, subtract two from the tables for long aisle space, and recalculate total chairs as the new tables count times ten. Return the number of tables and total chairs. Example: inputs 30, 20, and 100 returns 62.5 and 625.0.

title: Soap Fragrance Allocator
spec: Write a function `fragrance(oil, concentration, temperature)` for soap batching. Base fragrance is oil times concentration. If temperature is greater than forty, multiply the base fragrance by one point one for evaporation loss. Base water is oil times zero point three. If concentration is greater than zero point zero five, subtract the base fragrance from the base water. Total batch weight is oil plus base water plus base fragrance. Return the base fragrance, base water, and total batch weight. Example: inputs 100.0, 0.06, and 45.0 returns 6.6, 23.4, and 130.0.

title: Poultry Feed Projection
spec: Develop a function `feed(flock, age, mortality)` to estimate weekly farm feed. Base feed per bird is age times zero point zero five. Total daily feed is base feed times flock. Daily loss is flock times mortality. Surviving flock is flock minus daily loss. End of week feed per bird is surviving flock times age times zero point zero five plus zero point one. Weekly total feed is the total daily feed plus the end of week feed times three point five. If age is greater than ten, add twenty to the weekly total feed. Return the surviving flock and weekly total feed. Example: inputs 1000, 12, and 0.01 returns 990.0 and 2699.35.

title: Mulch Bed Volume
spec: Write a function `mulch(length, width, depth)` to quote landscaping materials. The area is length times width. Cubic feet is the area times depth. Cubic yards is cubic feet divided by twenty seven. If depth is less than zero point two, add zero point five to the cubic yards to account for uneven ground. Bags needed is cubic feet divided by two. Delivery cost starts at zero. If bags needed is greater than fifty, calculate the delivery cost as cubic yards times thirty plus fifty. Return the cubic yards, bags needed, and delivery cost. Example: inputs 10.0, 5.0, and 0.1 returns 0.685, 2.5, and 0.

title: Plasterboard Compound Estimator
spec: Create a function `compound(boards, taper)` to calculate drywall finishing materials. Joint length is boards times three. External corners is taper times two. Total length is joint length plus external corners. Base coat volume is total length times zero point two. Top coat volume is total length times zero point one. Total volume is base coat volume plus top coat volume. If taper is greater than five, add two to the total volume. Buckets required is total volume divided by fifteen. Return the base coat volume, top coat volume, and buckets required. Example: inputs 20 and 8 returns 15.2, 7.6, and 1.653.

title: Shipping Container Tiering
spec: Write a function `tiering(length, width, height)` to plan box loading. Boxes per row is twenty divided by length. Rows per tier is eight divided by width. Boxes per tier is boxes per row times rows per tier. Max tiers is eight point five divided by height. If height is greater than two, subtract one from max tiers for pallet clearance. Total boxes is boxes per tier times max tiers. Weight is total boxes times fifteen. Return the boxes per tier, max tiers, and total weight. Example: inputs 2.0, 1.0, and 2.5 returns 80.0, 2.4, and 2880.0.

title: Campground Firewood Stockpile
spec: Develop a function `firewood(sites, nights, temperature)` to stock a campsite. Fires per night is sites times zero point eight. Base hours per fire is four. If temperature is less than fifty, add two to the hours per fire. Wood per hour is zero point zero five. Wood per night is fires per night times hours per fire times wood per hour. Total wood is wood per night times nights. If total wood is greater than ten, add one to total wood for a reserve pile. Return fires per night, hours per fire, and total wood. Example: inputs 20, 3, and 40 returns 16.0, 6, and 15.4.

title: Orchard Blossom Thinning
spec: Write a function `thinning(trees, branches, blossoms)` for agricultural labor estimation. Total blossoms is trees times branches times blossoms. Target fruit per branch is blossoms divided by three. Retained blossoms is trees times branches times target fruit. Thinning amount is total blossoms minus retained blossoms. Labor hours is thinning amount divided by five hundred. If blossoms is greater than fifty, add the number of trees times two to the labor hours for high density work. Return retained blossoms, thinning amount, and labor hours. Example: inputs 10, 20, and 60 returns 4000.0, 8000.0, and 36.0.

title: Car Wash Chemical Dispensing
spec: Create a function `chemicals(vehicles, size, soil)` to measure cleaning agents. Base soap is vehicles times size times two. Base wax is vehicles times size times one. If soil is greater than three, multiply the base soap by one point five. If size is greater than two, add vehicles times zero point five to the base wax. Total chemicals is base soap plus base wax. Drums needed is total chemicals divided by fifty. Return the base soap, base wax, and drums needed. Example: inputs 100, 2.5, and 4 returns 750.0, 300.0, and 21.0.

title: Greenhouse Misting Schedule
spec: Write a function `misting(temp, humidity, sunlight)` to configure irrigation timers. Base duration is temp minus twenty. If humidity is less than fifty, add five to the base duration. Base frequency is sixty divided by sunlight. If temp is greater than thirty, divide the base frequency by two. Total water used is the base duration times twelve divided by base frequency. If total water is greater than one hundred, subtract ten from total water to prevent flooding. Return the base duration, base frequency, and total water. Example: inputs 35.0, 40.0, and 1.5 returns 20.0, 20.0, and 12.0.

title: Marathon Hydration Stations
spec: Develop a function `hydration(runners, temp, distance)` to plan race logistics. Stations needed is distance divided by two point five. Water per runner is temp times zero point zero two. Total water per station is runners times water per runner. Cups per station is total water per station divided by zero point one five. If temp is greater than twenty five, add runners times zero point five to the cups per station. Total cups is cups per station times stations needed. Return the stations needed, cups per station, and total cups. Example: inputs 1000, 30.0, and 25.0 returns 10.0, 4500.0, and 45000.0.

title: Farm Fencing Materials
spec: Write a function `fencing(length, width, strands)` to calculate wire and posts. Perimeter is length times two plus width times two. Posts needed is perimeter divided by ten. Wire length is perimeter times strands. If strands is greater than three, add posts needed times zero point five to the wire length for wrapping. The total cost is posts needed times five plus wire length times zero point one. Return the posts needed, wire length, and total cost. Example: inputs 100, 50, and 4 returns 30.0, 1215.0, and 271.5.

title: Book Binding Glue Estimator
spec: Create a function `binding(pages, thickness, copies)` for a print shop. Spine area is pages times thickness times zero point zero one. Base glue per book is spine area times zero point two. If pages is greater than three hundred, multiply base glue by one point two for side reinforcement. Total glue is base glue times copies. Waste allowance is total glue times zero point zero five. If copies is less than one hundred, set the waste allowance flatly to ten. Final glue is total glue plus waste allowance. Return the spine area, base glue per book, and final glue amount. Example: inputs 400, 2.0, and 50 returns 8.0, 1.92, and 106.0.

title: Donut Glaze Estimator
spec: Write a function `glaze(donuts, radius, thickness)` for a commercial bakery. Surface area is radius times radius times three point one four times two. Glaze per donut is surface area times thickness times zero point one. Base batch is donuts times glaze per donut. If radius is greater than four, add donuts times five to the base batch for dripping waste. Water needed is base batch times zero point two. Sugar needed is base batch times zero point eight. Return the surface area, water needed, and sugar needed. Example: inputs 100, 5.0, and 0.2 returns 157.0, 162.8, and 651.2.

title: Window Blind Fabric Cutting
spec: Develop a function `blinds(width, drop, windows)` to measure textile needs. Cut width is width plus ten. Cut drop is drop plus twenty. Base fabric length is cut drop times windows. If cut width is greater than one hundred and fifty, multiply the base fabric length by two because narrower rolls must be seamed. Hem allowance is windows times fifteen. Total length is the base fabric length plus hem allowance. Return the cut width, cut drop, and total length. Example: inputs 160.0, 100.0, and 2 returns 170.0, 120.0, and 510.0.

title: Plywood Formwork Design
spec: Write a function `formwork(height, rate, temp)` to determine concrete bracing. Concrete pressure is rate times temp times zero point five plus height. If concrete pressure is greater than fifty, cap the concrete pressure at fifty. Stud spacing is one thousand divided by concrete pressure. Tie spacing is stud spacing times two. If height is greater than three, subtract ten from tie spacing. Return the concrete pressure, stud spacing, and tie spacing. Example: inputs 4.0, 2.0, and 20.0 returns 24.0, 41.666, and 73.333.

title: Hydroponic Nutrient Dosing
spec: Create a function `dosing(volume, ec, ph)` to mix fertilizer tanks. Base nitrogen is volume times ec times two. Base phosphorus is volume times ec times zero point five. If ph is greater than six point five, multiply phosphorus by one point two to compensate for absorption lockout. Acid needed is the difference of ph minus five point eight, times volume times zero point one. If ec is less than one point five, add volume times five to the base nitrogen. Return the base nitrogen, base phosphorus, and acid needed. Example: inputs 100.0, 1.2, and 7.0 returns 740.0, 72.0, and 12.0.

title: Pallet Shrink Wrap Usage
spec: Write a function `shrinkwrap(pallets, height, girth)` for warehouse shipping. Wraps per pallet is height divided by zero point five. Base film length is wraps per pallet times girth. Overlap allowance is base film length times zero point two. If height is greater than two, add girth times two to the overlap allowance for top anchoring. Total film per pallet is base film length plus overlap allowance. Rolls needed is pallets times total film per pallet divided by five hundred. Return wraps per pallet, total film per pallet, and rolls needed. Example: inputs 10, 2.5, and 4.0 returns 5.0, 32.0, and 0.64.

title: Scaffold Board Deflection
spec: Develop a function `scaffold(span, load, thickness)` for site safety. Bending moment is load times span times span divided by eight. Inertia is thickness times thickness times thickness divided by twelve. Deflection is bending moment times five divided by inertia. If deflection is greater than span divided by one hundred, subtract one from span and recalculate the bending moment as load times the new span times the new span divided by eight. Boards required is load divided by fifty. Return the bending moment, inertia, and boards required. Example: inputs 105.0, 200.0, and 5.0 returns 270400.0, 10.416, and 4.0.

title: Drywall Screw Estimator
spec: Write a function `screws(boards, studs, thickness)` to count fasteners. Screws per board is studs times five plus ten. Base screws is boards times screws per board. If thickness is greater than fifteen, multiply base screws by one point two to account for double boarding. Waste is base screws times zero point one. Total screws is base screws plus waste. Boxes needed is total screws divided by one hundred. If boxes needed is less than two, set boxes needed to two. Return screws per board, total screws, and boxes needed. Example: inputs 20, 4, and 16.0 returns 30, 792.0, and 7.92.

title: Seismic Wave Velocity
spec: Write a function `analyze(depths)` that processes a list of rock layer thicknesses in meters. Calculate the primary wave travel time by assuming a surface velocity of three thousand meters per second, which increases by twenty meters per second for each meter of accumulated depth. Compute the secondary wave travel time which is the primary time multiplied by one point seven three. Keep a running total of the depth and travel times. If a layer thickness is less than ten meters, add a fixed delay of zero point zero five seconds to both times due to reflection boundaries. Return a tuple containing the total depth, total primary time, and total secondary time. Example input: a list with twenty, five, and fifty. Example output: seventy five, zero point zero two four, zero point zero four five.

title: Optical Fiber Dispersion
spec: Write a function `propagate(segments)` that takes a list of fiber optic cable lengths in kilometers. For each segment, calculate the chromatic dispersion assuming a dispersion parameter of seventeen picoseconds per nanometer kilometer. Calculate the pulse spreading based on a standard spectral width of zero point eight nanometers. If the pulse spread exceeds twenty picoseconds, subtract a compensation factor of five picoseconds. Add the spread of all segments to find the total pulse broadening. Also calculate the total signal attenuation assuming zero point two decibels per kilometer. Return a list containing the total distance, total pulse spread, and total attenuation. Example input: ten, twenty five, fifteen. Example output: fifty, sixty three point two, ten point zero.

title: Flywheel Energy Storage
spec: Write a function `evaluate(states)` that takes a list of rotational speeds in revolutions per minute. First convert each speed to radians per second by multiplying by pi and dividing by thirty. Calculate the kinetic energy stored in a cylindrical flywheel with a mass of five hundred kilograms and a radius of zero point six meters, where the moment of inertia is half the mass times the radius squared. If the energy is greater than one million joules, cap the usable energy by subtracting ten percent for safety margins. Calculate the power output if this usable energy is discharged uniformly over one hundred and twenty seconds. Return a tuple of the maximum kinetic energy found, the usable energy of the fastest state, and its power output. Example input: three thousand, four thousand. Output for four thousand: four million seven hundred thousand, four million two hundred thousand, thirty five thousand.

title: Subway Regenerative Braking
spec: Write a function `simulate(speeds)` that accepts a list of initial train speeds in meters per second. For each speed, calculate the kinetic energy of a train weighing forty thousand kilograms. During braking, assume the regenerative system recovers sixty percent of the energy. Calculate the stopping distance assuming a constant deceleration of one point two meters per second squared. The time to stop is the speed divided by the deceleration, and distance is half the deceleration times the time squared. If the stopping distance is greater than one hundred meters, the energy recovery efficiency drops by five percent due to heat generation. Return a list of tuples for each speed containing stopping distance and recovered energy in megajoules. Example input: fifteen, twenty. Example output for fifteen: ninety three point seven, five point four.

title: Ice Rink Refrigeration
spec: Write a function `refrigerate(temperatures)` that takes a list of outdoor air temperatures in Celsius. For an indoor ice rink of sixty meters by thirty meters, calculate the baseline heat load which is fifty thousand watts. For every degree the outdoor temperature is above ten degrees, add an additional heat load of two thousand five hundred watts. Calculate the compressor power required assuming a coefficient of performance of two point five, which means dividing the total heat load by this coefficient. If the outdoor temperature is below freezing, reduce the required power by fifteen percent. Calculate the daily energy consumption in kilowatt hours by multiplying by twenty four and dividing by one thousand. Return a list of daily energy values. Example input: five, fifteen, minus two. Output for fifteen: five hundred ninety five.

title: Laser Engraving Time
spec: Write a function `estimate(dimensions)` where the input is a list of tuples containing the width and height of designs in centimeters. For each design, calculate the total engraving distance assuming the laser sweeps back and forth with a line spacing of zero point zero one centimeters. The sweep length is the width, and the number of lines is the height divided by the spacing. The base time in seconds is the total distance divided by the laser speed of fifty centimeters per second. Add an acceleration overhead of zero point one seconds per line. If the width is greater than twenty centimeters, add a mechanical penalty of five percent to the time. Return the total time in minutes for each design. Example input: five and five. Example output: eight point seven five.

title: Tidal Bore Height
spec: Write a function `predict(depths)` taking a list of river depths in meters. The speed of a shallow water wave is the square root of the depth multiplied by gravity at nine point eight one. If the incoming tidal current speed, assumed to be five meters per second, is greater than the wave speed, a bore forms. The height of the bore is calculated as the Froude number squared minus one, multiplied by the depth, and divided by two. The Froude number is the tidal current divided by the wave speed. If no bore forms, the height is zero. Calculate the energy of the bore as the height squared multiplied by a constant of one thousand. Return a list of tuples containing the wave speed, bore height, and energy. Example input: two, three. Example output for two: four point four, zero point two nine, eighty four.

title: Ski Slope Grooming
spec: Write a function `schedule(trails)` taking a list of trail areas in square meters. A snowcat grooms at a speed of twelve kilometers per hour with a tiller width of four meters. First convert the speed to meters per hour. Calculate the grooming capacity in square meters per hour by multiplying the speed by the width and multiplying by zero point eight to account for overlap. The time required for each trail is the area divided by this capacity. If the trail area is less than ten thousand square meters, add a turning overhead of zero point five hours. Calculate fuel consumption assuming twenty five liters per hour. Return a tuple with the total grooming time and total fuel required across all trails. Example input: forty thousand, eight thousand. Example output: one point five four, thirty eight point five.

title: Cargo Drop Parachute
spec: Write a function `size(payloads)` that takes a list of cargo weights in kilograms. For each payload, calculate the required parachute area to achieve a safe landing velocity of six meters per second. The force of gravity is the weight multiplied by nine point eight one. The area is calculated as twice the gravitational force divided by the air density of one point two two multiplied by the square of the velocity, and then divided by a drag coefficient of one point five. If the payload is heavier than five hundred kilograms, multiply the area by a safety factor of one point two. Calculate the canopy diameter assuming a flat circular shape. Return a list of required diameters. Example input: one hundred, six hundred. Example output: four point three, twelve point two.

title: Welding Gas Consumption
spec: Write a function `calculate(welds)` that takes a list of weld lengths in centimeters. The travel speed of the welding torch is thirty centimeters per minute. Calculate the base welding time by dividing the length by the speed. Add a pre flow time of zero point one minutes and a post flow time of zero point one five minutes to every weld. The shielding gas flow rate is fifteen liters per minute. Calculate the gas used for each weld by multiplying the total time by the flow rate. If a weld length is less than ten centimeters, the post flow time increases to zero point two minutes to protect the cooling bead. Return the total gas consumed for all welds and the number of standard fifty liter cylinders needed, rounded up. Example input: fifty, five. Example output: twenty nine point two five, one.

title: Fiberglass Resin Mixture
spec: Write a function `batch(areas)` that processes a list of mold surface areas in square meters. A fiberglass layup requires one point five kilograms of glass mat per square meter. The resin to glass ratio by weight is two to one, so multiply the glass weight by two to find the resin weight. The hardener required is exactly two percent of the resin weight. If the ambient temperature is above twenty five degrees, reduce the hardener by ten percent to prevent premature curing. Calculate the total weight of the mixed batch by adding the resin and hardener. Return a list of tuples containing the resin weight and hardener weight for each area. Example input: two, five. Example output for two: six point zero, zero point one two.

title: Silo Grain Storage
spec: Write a function `capacity(heights)` where the input is a list of fill heights in meters for a cylindrical silo with a radius of four meters. Calculate the volume of grain by multiplying pi by the radius squared and by the height. The mass of the grain is the volume multiplied by the bulk density of seven hundred ninety kilograms per cubic meter. Calculate the pressure at the bottom of the silo using Janssen's equation approximated as the height multiplied by gravity and by the density, then reduced by twenty percent for wall friction. If the mass exceeds two hundred thousand kilograms, compute an overload penalty by adding ten kilopascals to the bottom pressure. Return a tuple containing the total mass across all heights and the maximum bottom pressure encountered. Example input: ten, fifteen. Example output: nine hundred fifty thousand, one hundred sixteen thousand.

title: Windlass Anchor Retrieval
spec: Write a function `retrieve(depths)` that processes a list of anchorage depths in meters. The anchor weighs twenty five kilograms and the chain weighs two point eight kilograms per meter. The total lifting force required is the anchor weight plus the chain weight, multiplied by gravity. The windlass motor lifts the anchor at a speed of zero point three meters per second. Calculate the mechanical power in watts as the force multiplied by the speed. The electrical power drawn from the twelve volt battery is the mechanical power divided by a motor efficiency of zero point seven five. Calculate the current draw in amps by dividing electrical power by twelve. If the depth is greater than thirty meters, add an extra ten amps due to water drag. Return a list of current draws for each depth. Example input: twenty, forty. Example output: twenty five point six, forty point five.

title: Compost Pile Aeration
spec: Write a function `aerate(volumes)` taking a list of compost pile volumes in cubic meters. Active composting requires zero point five cubic meters of air per hour for every cubic meter of compost. Calculate the required airflow rate. A standard blower provides thirty cubic meters of air per hour. Calculate the blower duty cycle as the required airflow divided by the blower capacity. If the volume is larger than forty cubic meters, the core temperature rises, requiring the duty cycle to be multiplied by one point two. Calculate the daily blower runtime in hours by multiplying the duty cycle by twenty four. Return a list of daily runtimes. Example input: ten, fifty. Example output: four point zero, twenty four point zero.

title: Fountain Pump Sizing
spec: Write a function `specify(heights)` taking a list of desired spray heights in meters. The theoretical pressure head required is the height plus ten percent for nozzle losses. The flow rate in liters per minute is calculated as the square root of the height multiplied by fifteen. Calculate the pipe friction loss as zero point zero five meters of head per liter per minute of flow. The total dynamic head is the pressure head plus the friction loss. If the total head exceeds fifteen meters, two pumps must be used in series, so divide the total head by two to find the head per pump. Calculate the pump power in watts by multiplying the flow rate by the head and by a constant factor of two point five. Return a list of tuples with flow rate and power per pump. Example input: four, nine. Example output for four: thirty, three hundred thirty.

title: Trampoline Spring Tension
spec: Write a function `analyze(weights)` that processes a list of jumper weights in kilograms. A trampoline has ninety six springs, each with a resting length of zero point one five meters and a spring constant of three thousand newtons per meter. The total downward force is the jumper weight multiplied by gravity, plus a dynamic multiplier of three for a hard bounce. The force is distributed equally among the springs. Calculate the stretch of each spring by dividing its share of the force by the spring constant. The extended length is the resting length plus the stretch. If the extended length is greater than zero point two meters, the spring is overextended and a safety flag is set to true. Return a list of tuples containing the extended length and the boolean flag. Example input: fifty, ninety. Example output for fifty: zero point one six five, false.

title: Aquaculture Biofilter Sizing
spec: Write a function `evaluate(biomass)` that takes a list of fish weights in kilograms for several tanks. Fish excrete thirty grams of ammonia per kilogram of feed, and feed rate is two percent of body weight per day. Calculate the daily ammonia production in grams. The biofilter bacteria can process zero point four grams of ammonia per square meter of media surface area per day. Calculate the required media surface area. Plastic biomedia provides five hundred square meters of surface area per cubic meter of volume. Calculate the required volume of biomedia. If the volume is less than zero point one cubic meters, set it to zero point one as a minimum operational size. Return a list of required biomedia volumes. Example input: one hundred, five hundred. Output for one hundred: zero point one two.

title: Chainsaw Kickback Energy
spec: Write a function `assess(speeds)` that accepts a list of engine speeds in revolutions per minute. The chainsaw sprocket has seven teeth and a chain pitch of three eighths of an inch. Convert the engine speed to chain speed in meters per second by multiplying by seven, multiplying by zero point zero one nine, and dividing by sixty. Calculate the kinetic energy of a sudden kickback assuming an effective moving mass of two point five kilograms, using the formula half mass times speed squared. If the energy is greater than one hundred joules, calculate the stopping time of the chain brake, which absorbs energy at a rate of five thousand watts. Return a list of tuples with chain speed and brake stopping time, using zero if no brake is needed. Example input: eight thousand, twelve thousand. Example output: seventeen point seven, zero point zero seven.

title: Moving Walkway Power
spec: Write a function `calculate(passengers)` taking a list of passenger counts on a walkway. The empty walkway requires a base power of four thousand watts to overcome friction. Each passenger adds an average mass of seventy five kilograms. The walkway moves at a speed of zero point six meters per second. Calculate the total passenger mass. The additional power required to move the passengers is the mass multiplied by gravity multiplied by a rolling resistance coefficient of zero point zero two and the speed. If the passenger count exceeds fifty, add a crowd friction factor of five hundred watts. Calculate the daily energy consumption assuming twelve hours of operation, converting watts to kilowatt hours. Return a list of daily energy usages. Example input: ten, sixty. Example output: fifty eight point six, seventy eight point four.

title: Zip Line Trajectory
spec: Write a function `model(weights)` taking a list of rider weights in kilograms. A zip line spans two hundred meters with a vertical drop of fifteen meters. Calculate the potential energy of the rider by multiplying weight, gravity, and the drop height. Assume friction consumes twenty percent of this energy. The remaining kinetic energy dictates the arrival speed, calculated as the square root of two times the kinetic energy divided by the mass. The braking system requires a distance equal to the kinetic energy divided by a maximum braking force of eight hundred newtons. If the arrival speed exceeds twenty meters per second, the braking force drops to six hundred newtons due to heat generation. Return a list of tuples containing speed and braking distance. Example input: sixty, ninety. Example output for sixty: fifteen point three, ten point six.

title: Tugboat Bollard Pull
spec: Write a function `estimate(displacements)` that processes a list of towed barge weights in metric tons. The hull resistance of the barge in newtons is calculated as the weight multiplied by one point five and added to the square of the towing speed, which is four meters per second. A basic propeller produces thrust equal to its shaft horsepower multiplied by one hundred and ten. Calculate the required horsepower to match the hull resistance. If the barge weight is over five thousand tons, the wake interaction increases resistance by fifteen percent, so multiply the required horsepower accordingly. Determine the thickness of the tow line needed by dividing the final resistance by a safe working load of two hundred newtons per square millimeter, then taking the square root. Return a list of tuples of horsepower and line thickness. Example input: three thousand, six thousand. Example output: forty one, four point seven.

title: Rotary Kiln Residence
spec: Write a function `simulate(speeds)` taking a list of rotation speeds in revolutions per minute for a cement kiln. The kiln is fifty meters long with a diameter of three meters and an incline slope of three degrees. The material residence time in minutes is calculated by multiplying the length by one point seven seven multiplied by the square root of the angle of repose which is thirty five degrees. Then divide this result by the product of the diameter, the slope, and the rotation speed. If the time is less than forty minutes, the material is undercooked, so calculate a recycle ratio of forty minus the time, divided by forty. If the time is adequate, the ratio is zero. Return a list of tuples containing the residence time and recycle ratio. Example input: one point five, two point five. Example output for one point five: thirty eight point eight, zero point zero three.

title: Sourdough Starter Hydration
spec: Write a function `balance(feedings)` taking a list of added flour weights in grams. A standard starter is kept at one hundred percent hydration, meaning equal parts water and flour by weight. Calculate the required water to match the added flour. The fermentation process consumes about five percent of the total weight as gas over twelve hours. Calculate the final weight after feeding and gas loss, assuming an initial starter weight of fifty grams before adding anything. If the final weight is less than one hundred grams, the mix is too small to sustain the colony, so compute an emergency top up of twenty grams of flour and twenty grams of water, recalculating the final weight. Return a list of total water added and final weights. Example input: twenty, forty. Example output for twenty: forty, one hundred twenty six.

title: Sausage Casing Length
spec: Write a function `compute(batches)` that takes a list of meat mixture volumes in cubic centimeters. A standard hog casing has a diameter of three point two centimeters. Calculate the cross sectional area by squaring half the diameter and multiplying by pi. The required length of casing in centimeters is the volume divided by this area. Each sausage link requires a twist that uses two centimeters of casing. Assuming a link is formed every fifteen centimeters of stuffed length, calculate the number of twists and multiply by two to get the total twist allowance. If the meat volume is greater than five thousand cubic centimeters, add an extra fifty centimeters of casing for handling waste. Return a list of tuples with total casing length and number of links for each batch. Example input: one thousand, six thousand. Example output for one thousand: one hundred forty one, eight.

title: Pneumatic Cylinder Force
spec: Write a function `evaluate(pressures)` that processes a list of operating air pressures in bar. Convert the pressure to newtons per square meter by multiplying by one hundred thousand. A pneumatic cylinder has a bore diameter of zero point zero five meters and a rod diameter of zero point zero two meters. Calculate the bore area and the rod area using pi. The extension force is the pressure multiplied by the bore area. The retraction force is the pressure multiplied by the difference between the bore area and the rod area. Calculate the air consumption in liters per stroke assuming a stroke length of zero point two meters, multiplying the bore area by the stroke and by the pressure in bar. If the extension force exceeds one thousand five hundred newtons, reduce the stroke length by zero point zero two meters to account for installing a physical stop. Return a list of tuples containing the extension forces and retraction forces. Example input: six, eight. Example output for six: one thousand one hundred seventy eight, nine hundred eighty nine.

title: Bowling Handicap Calculator
spec: Calculate bowling handicap scores. The entry function is `score(games)`. The input is a list of tuples containing game scratch scores and player averages. For each game, find the difference between two hundred and the player average. If this difference is greater than zero, the handicap is ninety percent of the difference. Otherwise, the handicap is zero. Truncate the handicap to an integer and add it to the scratch score to get the total. Find the highest total, lowest total, and average total.
