Returns a tuple of these three values. Example: an input of a tuple of one hundred and fifty and one hundred and forty should result in a handicap of fifty four and a total of two hundred and four.

title: Diving Competition Score
spec: Evaluate diving competition results. The entry function is `dive(results)`. The input is a list of tuples, where each tuple contains a list of seven judge scores and a difficulty degree. For each dive, sort the seven scores, remove the top two and bottom two, and sum the remaining three scores. Multiply this sum by the corresponding difficulty degree. If the difficulty is greater than three point zero, add a bonus of one point five to the dive score. Keep a running total of the overall score. Return the final total score rounded to two decimal places. Example: scores of seven across the board with a difficulty of two point zero yields a dive score of forty two.

title: Weightlifting Sinclair Total
spec: Adjust weightlifting totals across body weights. The entry function is `sinclair(lifts)`. The input is a list of tuples with body weight in kilograms and the total weight lifted. For each athlete, if their body weight is greater than or equal to one hundred and nine kilograms, the coefficient is exactly one. Otherwise, calculate the ratio of their body weight to one hundred and nine. Subtract this ratio from one, and square the result. Multiply this squared value by zero point seven nine, and calculate ten to the power of this product. Finally, multiply the total lifted by this coefficient. Return a list of adjusted totals rounded to one decimal place.

title: Track and Field Decathlon
spec: Calculate decathlon points for specific events. The entry function is `decathlon(performances)`. The input is a list of tuples with the event type as a plain string, either longjump or shotput, and the performance metric. For the long jump, points are zero point one four multiplied by the result of the performance minus two hundred and twenty, all raised to the power of one point four. For the shot put, points are fifty one point three multiplied by the result of the performance minus one point five, all raised to the power of one point zero five. Truncate the calculated points to an integer. Accumulate and return the total points across all events.

title: Cycling Power Profile
spec: Analyze cycling power output. The entry function is `cycling(watts)`. The input is a list of power values in watts recorded every second. Calculate the rolling average over thirty seconds for the entire list. Find the maximum thirty second average. Then determine the percentage of the total time the power was greater than three hundred watts. Count the number of seconds the power was less than one hundred watts. Return a tuple containing the maximum thirty second average, the percentage over three hundred watts, and the count of seconds under one hundred watts.

title: Rowing Ergometer Split
spec: Convert rowing ergometer intervals to paces and watts. The entry function is `rowing(intervals)`. The input is a list of tuples with distance in meters and time in seconds. For each interval, calculate the speed in meters per second. The pace per five hundred meters is five hundred divided by the speed. If the pace is less than one hundred and twenty seconds, it is classified as a sprint. Calculate the average power in watts using the formula two point eight divided by the cube of the pace divided by five hundred. Return a list of tuples containing the pace in seconds and the calculated watts.

title: Sailing Handicap Scoring
spec: Adjust sailing race times using a yardstick rating. The entry function is `sailing(results)`. The input is a list of tuples with elapsed time in seconds and the yardstick rating. Calculate the corrected time by multiplying the elapsed time by one hundred and dividing by the yardstick rating. If the corrected time is less than three thousand seconds, subtract a bonus of fifty seconds from it. Find the minimum corrected time among all boats. Return a list of differences between each boat's corrected time and the winning minimum time.

title: Equestrian Show Jumping
spec: Score equestrian show jumping rounds. The entry function is `jumping(rounds)`. The input is a list of tuples with time taken in seconds and the number of knocked rails. The optimum time is eighty five seconds. For every second over the optimum time, add zero point two five time penalties. Each knocked rail adds four jumping penalties. The total penalty is the sum of time and jumping penalties. If the total penalty is exactly zero and the time is less than eighty seconds, the round is a fast clear round. Return a tuple with the number of fast clear rounds and the average total penalties across all rounds.

title: Surfing Wave Evaluation
spec: Evaluate judge scores for surfing waves. The entry function is `surfing(waves)`. The input is a list of lists, where each inner list contains five judge scores for a wave. For each wave, remove the highest and lowest scores, then average the remaining three. A wave is considered excellent if this average is greater than or equal to eight. Keep the highest two wave averages for each surfer to form their heat total by adding them together. Return a list of the heat totals for all surfers.

title: Golf Handicap Index
spec: Calculate a golf handicap index from recent rounds. The entry function is `handicap(rounds)`. The input is a list of tuples containing the gross score, course rating, and slope rating. For each round, subtract the course rating from the gross score, multiply by one hundred and thirteen, and divide by the slope rating to find the differential. Sort the differentials from lowest to highest. If there are fewer than five rounds, use only the lowest differential. If there are five or more rounds, average the lowest three differentials. Multiply the chosen value or average by zero point nine six. Return the final index.

title: Basketball Efficiency Rating
spec: Calculate basketball player efficiency ratings. The entry function is `efficiency(stats)`. The input is a list of tuples with points, rebounds, assists, steals, blocks, missed field goals, and turnovers. For each player, add the first five statistical categories together. Subtract the missed field goals and subtract the turnovers to get the efficiency rating. If the rating is greater than twenty, it is a star performance. If the rating is less than ten, it is a poor performance. Return a tuple containing the maximum rating, the minimum rating, and the total count of star performances.

title: Football Passer Rating
spec: Compute the passer rating for football quarterbacks. The entry function is `passer(stats)`. The input is a tuple of attempts, completions, passing yards, touchdowns, and interceptions. Calculate the percentage of completions by dividing completions by attempts, subtract zero point three, and multiply by five. Calculate yards per attempt by dividing yards by attempts, subtract three, and multiply by zero point two five. Calculate touchdowns per attempt by dividing touchdowns by attempts and multiplying by twenty. Calculate interceptions per attempt, multiply by twenty five, and subtract from two point three seven five. If any of these four values is greater than two point three seven five, cap it at that value; if less than zero, set it to zero. Add the four values, divide by six, and multiply by one hundred. Return the rating.

title: Soccer League Standings
spec: Process a soccer team's match results to determine their standing. The entry function is `standings(matches)`. The input is a list of tuples for one team, containing goals scored and goals conceded in each match. A win is when goals scored is greater than goals conceded and awards three points. A draw is when goals scored equals goals conceded and awards one point. A loss awards zero points. The goal difference for a match is goals scored minus goals conceded. Accumulate the total points and total goal difference. Return a tuple of total points, total goal difference, and the win percentage calculated as wins divided by total matches multiplied by one hundred.

title: Marathon Pace Pacing
spec: Analyze marathon split times for pacing strategies. The entry function is `marathon(splits)`. The input is a list of times in seconds for five kilometer segments. The total distance is forty two point one nine five kilometers. For each segment, calculate the pace in seconds per kilometer by dividing the time by five. Compare the average pace of the second half of the race, which is the last four segments, to the first half, which is the first four segments. If the second half average pace is less than the first half, it is a negative split. Calculate the estimated finish time by scaling the total time so far by the ratio of the full distance to the distance covered. Return a tuple with a boolean for negative split and the projected finish time.

title: Triathlon Transition Timing
spec: Evaluate transition efficiency in a triathlon. The entry function is `triathlon(athletes)`. The input is a list of tuples containing swim time, transition one time, bike time, transition two time, and run time, all in minutes. The total time is the sum of all five components. The transition percentage is the sum of both transition times divided by the total time, multiplied by one hundred. If the bike time is greater than double the run time, the athlete is flagged as a strong runner. Return a list of tuples containing the total time, transition percentage, and the strong runner boolean for each athlete.

title: Biathlon Pursuit Penalty
spec: Calculate the total course time for a biathlon pursuit. The entry function is `biathlon(shootings)`. The input is a list of tuples with the shooting time in seconds and the number of missed targets for each bout. The base course time is twelve hundred seconds. For each shooting bout, add the shooting time to the total. For every missed target, add a penalty loop time of twenty two point five seconds. The total penalty time is the sum of all missed targets multiplied by twenty two point five. If the total penalty time is greater than one hundred seconds, add an additional mental fatigue penalty of fifteen seconds. Return the final total time.

title: Fencing Pool Bout Ranking
spec: Rank fencing bouts in a preliminary pool. The entry function is `fencing(bouts)`. The input is a list of tuples with touches scored and touches received for a fencer. A bout is counted as a victory if touches scored equals five, or if touches scored is greater than touches received. Calculate the total number of victories. The indicator is the total touches scored minus the total touches received. The win rate is victories divided by the total number of bouts. If the win rate is greater than zero point eight and the indicator is greater than ten, flag the fencer as a top seed. Return a tuple of victories, indicator, win rate, and the top seed boolean.

title: Bobsled Push Velocity
spec: Analyze the push phase of a bobsled run. The entry function is `bobsled(pushes)`. The input is a list of split times in seconds at ten, twenty, and thirty meters. Calculate the velocity for the first ten meters by dividing ten by the first split. Calculate the velocity between ten and twenty meters by dividing ten by the difference between the second and first splits. Calculate the velocity between twenty and thirty meters similarly. Find the maximum of these three velocities. Calculate the acceleration between the first two zones by dividing the velocity difference by the time difference. Finally, calculate the estimated kinetic energy at thirty meters using a sled mass of two hundred and ten multiplied by the square of the last interval velocity, divided by two. Return a tuple of maximum velocity, acceleration, and kinetic energy.

title: Gymnastics Event Scoring
spec: Calculate final scores for gymnastics routines. The entry function is `gymnastics(routines)`. The input is a list of tuples containing a start difficulty value, a list of five execution deductions, and a neutral deduction penalty. For each routine, subtract all five execution deductions from a base score of ten. Add the start difficulty value to this execution score. Subtract the neutral deduction penalty. If the resulting execution score before adding difficulty is less than seven point five, subtract an additional zero point three for overall poor execution. Find and return the highest final score from the list of routines.

title: Snooker Break Builder
spec: Track points during a snooker break. The entry function is `snooker(pots)`. The input is a list of string colors representing consecutive balls potted. Red is worth one point, yellow two, green three, brown four, blue five, pink six, and black seven. Start with a score of zero. Iterate through the potted balls. If the current ball is red and the previous ball was also red, a foul occurred; subtract four points instead of adding. Otherwise, add the point value of the ball. If the total score goes above one hundred and forty seven, it is an invalid break. Calculate the average points per pot. Return a tuple of the total score and the average.

title: Archery Tournament Scoring
spec: Score arrows in an archery tournament based on distance from the center. The entry function is `archery(arrows)`. The input is a list of distances from the center in centimeters. Calculate the score for each arrow as eleven minus the distance divided by two and rounded up to an integer. If the calculated score is greater than ten, cap it at ten. If the score is less than zero, set it to zero. If the distance is less than or equal to zero point five, it is considered an inner ten. Sum the total score across all arrows. Count the number of inner tens. Return a tuple of the total score and the inner ten count.

title: Tennis Serve Statistics
spec: Analyze tennis serve performance. The entry function is `serve(serves)`. The input is a list of tuples containing serve speed in miles per hour, a boolean for whether it was a fault, and a boolean for whether the point was won. Calculate the percentage of valid serves, which are those that are not faults. For all valid serves, find the maximum speed and the average speed. Calculate the win percentage on valid serves by dividing the won points by the number of valid serves. If the win percentage is greater than zero point seven and the average speed is greater than one hundred and ten, flag it as an excellent serving day. Return a tuple of valid percentage, average speed, win percentage, and the excellent boolean.

title: Shooting Range Target Analysis
spec: Evaluate shot placements on a shooting range target. The entry function is `target(shots)`. The input is a list of tuples providing horizontal and vertical coordinates in inches from the center of the bullseye. For each shot, calculate the radial distance from the center as the square root of the horizontal coordinate squared plus the vertical coordinate squared. If this distance is less than or equal to one inch, it scores ten points. Otherwise, it scores five points. Calculate the average horizontal offset and average vertical offset across all shots. If the absolute value of the average horizontal offset is greater than two inches, a windage adjustment is needed. Return a tuple of total points, maximum radial distance, and a boolean for windage adjustment.
